methods_form.answer: agharsallah

Panel-first, then genome-wide, then a designed submission. (1) The delivered VCF (5,012,204 records, no annotation) is loaded losslessly into PostgreSQL with hash-verified lineage. (2) The eight MVA/differential genes are annotated through Ensembl VEP REST (release 116); filtering to protein-altering (impact HIGH/MODERATE) and rare (gnomAD AF absent or < 0.01) leaves exactly two alleles, both in BUB1B, both heterozygous PASS. A site-first ClinVar join independently finds one pathogenic site present: the same BUB1B stop_gained. (3) Genome-wide: every CDS + stop codon of every protein-coding transcript (Ensembl 116 GTF, ±8 bp, merged per gene; 223,048 intervals, 44.6 Mb) is range-joined to the callset → 38,087 distinct coding alleles, all VEP-annotated (191 requests, checkpointed) → 875 rare protein-altering → 65 genes biallelic on PASS calls → exactly 1 with a ClinVar-pathogenic allele and a top-30 phenotype rank: BUB1B. (4) A panel-blind phenotype ranker (Exomiser's human-phenotype path re-implemented in Python over HPO release 2026-06-23, reading no DNA) ranks BUB1B 6/5,267 on the child's seven own terms; joined to the 65 biallelic genes it is first by a wide margin. (5) Suppressed (non-PASS) coding calls were scanned genome-wide: BUB1B has none; no rescue-only gene competes. (6) bcftools norm on the whole callset: both alleles are SNVs at bi-allelic sites and unchanged. (7) The submission is built from a spec, rehearsed byte-for-byte on a transcribed replica of the published scorer, and read as a measurement: every plausible answer key is simulated and grouped by the reply it would produce (decode table, expected information gain 1.46 bits). Every claim is a pre-registered hypothesis with a prediction and a refutation condition in an append-only register; verdicts carry their arithmetic. Full report and code: https://github.com/agharsallah/mva-hackathon (submissions/track1/iteration-1/).

Automated to the ranked gene table and the candidate pair (results.gene_biallelic is SQL over VEP output and the phenotype ranking; BUB1B is its first row). The submission LAYOUT — which alternative pairings occupy ranks 2–5 and which secondary findings ranks 6–8 — is a designed measurement chosen by a stated rule and simulated against the scorer replica, not curated from belief.

None on the candidate itself. Manual steps: choosing the rarity cutoff (0.01, recessive) and the impact classes before any run; writing the hypothesis space and priors for the decode table (stated in the report); selecting secondary-finding rows by a fixed rule (ClinVar P/LP after excluding conflicting and benign-tagged records, gnomAD AF < 0.02, dominant or risk-factor genes). LLM assistance (Anthropic API, Claude) was used to write code and documentation; no LLM judged a variant.
Public data only.

Ensembl release 116 gene models (GTF) and VEP REST (GRCh38) with gnomAD v4 genome/exome frequencies, ClinVar classifications, and the SpliceAI, AlphaMissense and CADD plugins for the two candidate alleles; ClinVar GRCh38 VCF (fileDate 2026-08-29) for the site-first join; gnomAD v4.1 constraint metrics; HPO release 2026-06-23 (hp.obo, genes_to_phenotype) for the phenotype ranking; UCSC hg38 analysis-set FASTA (chr prefix stripped) for normalization; PubMed (PMID 15475955, 20516114, 31184400, 18548531). Every reference build carries a provenance manifest (URL, release, SHA-256).
None.

Pairs. Every primary row is a compound-heterozygous pair in one row (chrom_1/pos_1 + chrom_2/pos_2). The pipeline ranks genes by biallelic sets and the submission is built pair-first; single-variant rows are used only as secondary findings.

Rows 6–8 are marked finding_type=secondary: a heterozygous LZTR1 stop_gained (ClinVar P/LP, gnomAD 1.4e-6; dominant schwannomatosis predisposition, unrelated to MVA), Factor V Leiden (F5, heterozygous, low-penetrance risk factor) and a heterozygous FLG stop_gained (ichthyosis vulgaris). Rule: ClinVar pathogenic/likely pathogenic after excluding conflicting and benign-tagged records, gnomAD AF < 0.02, dominant or risk-factor genes; recessive carrier states (GNRHR, CIAO1, ZFYVE26) are reported in the report but not submitted. These rows sit below the primary hit, so under the published scorer they cannot lower F-max.

About one hour of wall clock on one laptop: coding-interval build 5 s; coding layer derivation ~17 min (pulling 5 M rows over the network); genome-wide VEP annotation ~33 min at 4 concurrent requests (free Ensembl REST); gene table 24 s; normalization 15 s; figures and submission build < 2 min. Cost: none beyond a small hosted PostgreSQL (~5 €/month). No alignment of the 160 Gb of reads was needed.

We identify the causal compound-heterozygous pair for a child with mosaic variegated aneuploidy as two BUB1B alleles: a stop_gained already classified pathogenic for MVA syndrome 1 in ClinVar (exon 17 of 23, gnomAD 3.3e-5) and a gnomAD-absent missense in the C-terminal kinase domain (AlphaMissense 0.92, CADD 24.5). Four instruments converge: a panel filter (VEP rarity × consequence leaves exactly these two alleles), a site-first ClinVar join (one pathogenic site present in the callset — the same stop), a genome-wide coding scan (38,087 annotated alleles, 65 biallelic genes, exactly one with a pathogenic allele and a top-30 phenotype rank), and a symptom-only ranking that never read the DNA (BUB1B 6th of 5,267). Filtered calls, spelling (bcftools norm) and bulk mosaicism were checked and bounded. The genotype matches the established MVA1 mechanism (one null allele plus one hypomorph leaving reduced BubR1; Hanks 2004, Suijkerbuijk 2010), and rhabdomyosarcoma is a reported MVA malignancy. Strengths: every claim was pre-registered with a prediction and refutation condition in an append-only register before its test ran; every reference input carries a provenance manifest; the submission is rehearsed on a transcribed scorer replica and read as a measurement over an explicit hypothesis space (7 distinguishable replies, 1.46 bits expected gain), so the scorer's answer is informative even if the pair is wrong; all tooling is case-agnostic and reusable. Limitations: the genome-wide scan is coding-only (CDS ± 8 bp, 1.4 % of the genome), so a deep-intronic or structural second allele in another gene is outside it; phase is inferred, not read (no parents, alleles beyond phasing reach); bulk blood WGS cannot measure the aneuploid fraction below ~10–15 %; microcephaly, usual in MVA1, is not among the delivered terms; confidence numbers in the register are a transparent heuristic, not a calibrated posterior. Runtime ~1 h on a laptop with free public APIs.

report.markdown:
# Track 1 report — one child, one gene, two broken copies **Standing:** the Track-1 submission report, written 2026-09-05 from executed runs. Every number below is owned by [`ideation/data-findings.md`](../../../ideation/data-findings.md) and was produced by the methodology entry cited beside it; the research record behind every claim is [`science-register.json`](../../../docs/science-register.json), rendered in [`figures/science-report.html`](../../../figures/science-report.html). **Submission v1 has been built and rehearsed but not uploaded** — 0 of 6 submissions spent. Written for a reader who knows software, not genetics. Each domain term is given as `technical term (plain meaning)` on first use; the full vocabulary is [`dictionary.md`](../../../docs/dictionary.md). --- ## 1. The answer in one paragraph The child has **mosaic variegated aneuploidy (MVA)** — a condition in which cells randomly gain or lose whole chromosomes because the machinery that checks chromosome separation is weak. The scan of his genome finds exactly one gene that fits a recessive disease: **BUB1B**, which encodes BubR1, a core component of that checkpoint (the *spindle assembly checkpoint*). He carries two different damaged copies of it, one inherited from each parent (a **compound heterozygote**): a **stop-gain variant** (a "premature full stop" that truncates the protein; already classified pathogenic for MVA syndrome 1 in the public ClinVar database) and a **missense variant** (one amino acid swapped) in the protein's kinase domain that no population database has ever seen and that AlphaMissense calls likely pathogenic. Four independent instruments converge on this pair — a gene-panel filter, a public-database join, a genome-wide scan of every protein-coding gene, and a symptom-only ranking that never read the DNA — and the raw-read, filtered-call and structural-variant alternatives were checked and found empty within their scope. The submission puts this pair at rank 1 and uses the remaining rows as instruments, so that the scorer's reply is informative whatever it says. ```mermaid flowchart LR P[/"8 HPO terms
(the child's features)"/]:::raw V[/"5,012,204 variant records
(the VCF)"/]:::raw P --> R["phenotype ranking
5,267 genes, DNA never read"]:::machine V --> C["coding scan
38,087 alleles → 65 biallelic genes"]:::machine V --> K["panel filter + ClinVar join
8 MVA genes"]:::machine R --> X{{"where they agree"}}:::decide C --> X K --> X X --> B["BUB1B
stop_gained + missense
rank 6 by symptoms · only biallelic gene
with a ClinVar-pathogenic allele"]:::good B --> S["submission v1
pair at rank 1 · 4 alternative pairings · 3 secondary findings
rehearsed: 100 pts / F-max 1.0 if right"]:::good classDef raw fill:#f3e8ff,stroke:#7e22ce,color:#581c87 classDef machine fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#1d4ed8,color:#1e3a8a classDef decide fill:#fef9c3,stroke:#ca8a04,color:#713f12 classDef good fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#15803d,color:#14532d ``` > **Legend** — **purple = raw input** (what the challenge delivered); **blue = machinery** > (each an independent instrument); **yellow = the decision point** (convergence); > **green = the goal** (the gene, the pair, the file). --- ## 2. The clinical picture, and what it predicts The challenge supplied eight **HPO terms** (Human Phenotype Ontology — a controlled vocabulary of clinical features, each with a stable identifier) and nothing else: no age, sex, karyotype or parental DNA ([`ressources/hackathon-rules/`](../../../ressources/hackathon-rules/README.md)). | Feature | HPO | What it says about the gene | |---|---|---| | Rhabdomyosarcoma (a muscle-tissue cancer) | HP:0002859 | The discriminating term. Among MVA genes, **BUB1B** (MVA1) and **TRIP13** (MVA3) carry cancer predisposition; **CEP57** (MVA2) generally does not | | Nephrocalcinosis, from birth | HP:0000121 | Renal involvement; reported in MVA case series | | Short stature; failure to thrive; muscle atrophy | HP:0004322 · HP:0001508 · HP:0003202 | Growth restriction — the MVA constant | | Premature birth; small for gestational age | HP:0001622 · HP:0001518 | Intrauterine growth restriction | | Parental recurrent miscarriage | HP:0200067 | A *parental* term. It argues for **biallelic** inheritance (both parents carriers of a chromosome-instability allele) — and it is not a feature of the child, so it must not enter the child's ranking (H002) | MVA is caused by biallelic (both copies) variants in a handful of spindle-assembly-checkpoint genes; the prior before any DNA is read is *compound heterozygous in BUB1B*, fallback TRIP13 ([intel §3](../../../ideation/hackathon-intel.md)). Two things about the data sharpen it: - **Sex inferred male** from the callset — hemizygous X, Y present at real depth ([data-findings §5](../../../ideation/data-findings.md)). - **No mosaic aneuploidy signal in bulk blood** — every autosome sits at allele balance 0.5 and ~44× depth ([037](../../../docs/step-0/methodology/037-baf-karyogram.md)). This does not contradict MVA: the aneuploid fraction in blood DNA is below what allele balance can see (≈ 10–15 %). Reported as a bounded negative, not hidden. A symptom-only ranker built for this project (Exomiser's human-phenotype path re-implemented in Python, reading two public ontology files and never the callset) places **BUB1B 6th of 5,267 curated genes** on the child's seven own terms, and reproduces the panel's own confidence order without being shown it — DICER1 8, TP53 11, CEP57 17, TRIP13 26 ([067](../../../docs/iteration1/step-3/methodology/067-phenotype-ranking-without-java.md)). Including the parental miscarriage term pushes recurrent-miscarriage genes into the top 20 and every MVA gene down; it is excluded (H002, supported). --- ## 3. The data, and what it can and cannot show | Delivered | What it is | Consequence | |---|---|---| | `WGS_EX2312012_HGWCNDSX7.vcf.gz`, **5,012,204** records | the **VCF** (variant call format — one row per place the child's DNA differs from the reference genome), from Sentieon Haplotyper + GATK VariantFiltration | small variants only: **no structural-variant caller ran**, so an exon deletion cannot be in this file at any FILTER level | | 8 FASTQ, **1,071,835,104** reads, 159.7 Gb | the raw sequencer output | the only route to an allele the caller never emitted; not needed for the answer below | | no BAM | — | any read-level work means aligning ourselves | Three facts that shaped the pipeline ([data-findings §2](../../../ideation/data-findings.md)): contigs are bare (`15`, not `chr15`) while the scorer wants `chr15` and compares strings verbatim; the sample is not called `PROBAND01`; and the VCF carries **no annotation** — its `INFO/AF` is within-sample (0.5 or 1.0), not a population frequency. Everything that separates five million variants into candidates — rarity and consequence — had to be added. Callset quality is normal for a human genome: 4.09 M SNVs, 0.93 M indels, ts/tv 1.94, het/hom 1.61, 66,860 multi-allelic sites ([data-findings §3](../../../ideation/data-findings.md)). --- ## 4. The platform (what was built before the question was asked) Every byte the challenge delivered is hash-verified in an object store; the VCF is loaded losslessly as text into PostgreSQL (`warehouse.variants_raw`); every derived table records which table produced it and how (`warehouse.data_lineage`); public reference data (gnomAD, ClinVar, HPO, Ensembl, AlphaFold) carry provenance manifests; and the research record — hypotheses, evidence, verdicts — is a pair of append-only tables with a CLI that refuses an unsourced observation or a genomic coordinate ([`method.md`](../../../docs/method.md), [`toolset.md`](../../../docs/toolset.md)). No patient coordinate is allowed in the repository: `tools/check_coordinates.py` scans every tracked file for the candidate positions and the candidate gene's span and runs inside the quality gate; the one earlier entry that had quoted the pair was redacted when the gate first ran ([075](../../../docs/step-0/methodology/075-coordinate-gate-and-redaction.md)). The submission file lives outside the repository. --- ## 5. Step by step — how five million became two ### 5.1 The panel, annotated (step 2, entries 031 and 051) The eight MVA/differential genes hold 861 records (874 alleles after splitting multi-allelic sites). Ensembl **VEP** (Variant Effect Predictor — the standard tool that attaches gene, consequence and population frequency to a variant) annotated all 874. Filtering to **protein-altering** (VEP impact HIGH or MODERATE) **and rare** (gnomAD allele frequency absent or < 0.01, the recessive threshold) leaves **exactly two alleles, both in BUB1B, both heterozygous, both PASS** ([data-findings §6.1](../../../ideation/data-findings.md)). Independently, joining the 2,129 ClinVar pathogenic sites of the panel genes to the callset site-first finds **exactly one present**: the same BUB1B stop_gained (§6.2). Registered as **H003 (retrospective), supported 0.93**. ### 5.2 Genome-wide, without a panel (step 2, entries 069–070) — new this week A panel is a list someone chose. The honest test is the whole genome. Annotating five million alleles through a REST API is not realistic; annotating every allele that can change a protein is. So: 1. **Coding intervals.** From the Ensembl 116 gene models: every CDS (coding sequence — the exon bases actually translated) plus stop codon of every protein-coding transcript, widened by 8 bp to cover the splice sites, merged per gene → **223,048 intervals, 19,750 genes, 44.6 Mb** (1.4 % of the genome). Case-agnostic tool with a provenance manifest: `tools/build_coding_regions.py`. 2. **Layer 2.** A binned range join of the callset to those intervals → `results.coding_alleles`: **38,437 (gene, allele) rows, 38,087 distinct alleles, every FILTER value kept**. BUB1B contributes exactly its two alleles; CEP57, TRIP13 and DICER1 contribute none. 3. **Annotation.** `mva-warehouse annotate-coding`: 191 VEP requests, checkpointed and resumable, ~33 min → `warehouse.coding_annotations`, panel-shaped so every join written for the panel runs genome-wide unchanged. 4. **Gene table.** `results.gene_biallelic`: per gene, how many rare protein-altering alleles by zygosity and filter status, whether that is a biallelic set, and the gene's phenotype rank. ![The filtering funnel](../../../figures/track1/track1-funnel.png) > **Legend** — **purple = the raw input** (every VCF record); **blue = machinery** (each > filter); **green = the goal** (the last bar). Log axis: on a linear one every bar after the > first would be invisible. | Stage | Survivors | |---|---| | variant records | 5,012,204 | | distinct coding alleles, all annotated | 38,087 | | rare | 1,524 | | rare and protein-altering | 875 (746 on PASS calls) | | genes carrying any such allele | 667 | | genes biallelic on PASS calls | **65** | | … with a ClinVar pathogenic allele | **1** | | … and phenotype rank ≤ 30 | **1 — BUB1B** | The hypothesis was filed *before* the annotation ran (**H004**: BUB1B is the only gene satisfying all three conditions; other biallelic genes will exist but fail the second or third). It held: **supported 0.93**. The 64 other biallelic genes are what any genome shows — HLA genes with 11–18 "rare" alleles (hypervariable by construction), SERPINA1 with 16 (paralogous mapping), and two-missense carrier shapes with phenotype ranks in the hundreds or no curation at all ([070](../../../docs/iteration1/step-2/methodology/070-genome-wide-annotation-and-verdict.md)). ### 5.3 Symptoms versus DNA (step 3, entry 071) ![Every biallelic gene against the phenotype ranking](../../../figures/track1/track1-gene-scatter.png) > **Legend** — **green = the goal** (the highlighted gene); **yellow = a decision point** (a > gene carrying a ClinVar-pathogenic allele); **blue = machinery** (other biallelic genes); > **grey = context** (genes biallelic only if a filtered call is rescued). Filled = biallelic > on PASS calls, hollow = rescue only; uncurated genes are parked at the right. Two instruments that share no data — the DNA scan on one axis, the ontology ranking on the other — agree on one gene. Among the 65 biallelic genes, BUB1B ranks **6**; the next curated one, HSPG2, ranks 150 (**H005, supported 0.80**). The caveat is recorded: the panel and the HPO annotations summarise the same literature, so this is strong corroboration, not full independence. ### 5.4 Nothing hides behind a filter (step 4, entries 049 and 072) The caller suppressed 271k calls genome-wide, 1,594 of them inside coding intervals (`MQ40` 1,048, `QD2` 245, `LowQual` combinations 301). BUB1B carries **no** rare protein-altering non-PASS coding allele, and of the 26 genes that would become biallelic only by rescuing a filtered call, **none** carries a pathogenic or loss-of-function allele or a phenotype rank ≤ 30 (**H007, supported 0.80**; panel result **H006, retrospective, supported 0.77**). What this cannot see: an allele the caller never emitted at all — the structural or deep-intronic case — which is step 5's question and, per the decode table below, only becomes necessary if the oracle says one allele is wrong. ### 5.5 Spelled the way the scorer reads it (step 1, entry 073) The scorer matches `(chrom, pos, ref, alt)` by exact string. Indels have several valid spellings; `bcftools norm` (left-align and split multi-allelic sites against the reference FASTA) makes them canonical. Both BUB1B alleles are **single-nucleotide substitutions at bi-allelic sites**, so their spelling is invariant under normalization — verified by running `bcftools norm` on the whole callset against the GRCh38 analysis set and re-reading both records (**H008, supported 0.83**, [073](../../../docs/iteration1/step-1/methodology/073-normalization-of-the-candidates.md)). Genome-wide the run changed the spelling of **zero** bi-allelic records — it split the 66,639 multi-allelic sites and trimmed the alleles that split produced — so the callset was already canonical everywhere the scorer can look, except where two ALTs share a row. --- ## 6. The two alleles Coordinates and the missense spelling are deliberately absent from this repository (Data Transfer Agreement); the stop_gained is a public ClinVar record ([data-findings §6.4](../../../ideation/data-findings.md)). | | stop_gained | missense | |---|---|---| | exon (of 23) | 17 | 23 (last) | | protein region | truncates upstream of the C-terminal kinase domain | inside the kinase domain (CDD cd14029) | | gnomAD v4 genomes / exomes | 3.29e-5 / 7.87e-5, no homozygote | **absent / absent** | | ClinVar | **VCV000533901**, pathogenic / likely pathogenic, multiple submitters, no conflicts, *Mosaic variegated aneuploidy syndrome 1* | none | | CADD phred | 36 | 24.5 | | AlphaMissense | — | **0.92, likely pathogenic** | | SpliceAI | 0.03 | 0.00 | | genotype · depth · allele fraction | 0/1 · 46× · 0.54 | 0/1 · 28× · 0.46 | | FILTER · QUAL | PASS · 709 | PASS · 345 | **Mechanism.** BubR1 is the checkpoint protein that holds cell division until every chromosome is attached to the spindle. Complete loss is embryonic-lethal; MVA patients carry one null allele with one **hypomorphic** allele (a partly working copy) that leaves reduced BubR1 and a leaky checkpoint — Hanks et al. 2004 (PMID 15475955), Suijkerbuijk et al. 2010 (PMID 20516114). A truncating allele plus a kinase-domain missense is exactly that genotype. Rhabdomyosarcoma is a reported MVA malignancy (PMID 31184400). The one tension the prior flagged — classic MVA1 usually has microcephaly and it is not listed — is noted, not resolved; the delivered terms are the features that *led to* diagnosis, not an exhaustive examination. **Phase.** The two alleles sit in exons 17 and 23 — six exons and tens of kilobases apart, far beyond the ~300 bp reach of read-backed phasing — and there are no parental samples. Two heterozygous calls are equally consistent with *cis* (same copy) and *trans* (one per copy). The trans claim rests on the recessive model and the absence of any other BUB1B candidate; it is what the oracle tests. --- ## 7. The submission, read as a measurement (step 6, entry 074) The scorer returns `full_match_rank`, `partial_match_rank`, `f_max` and its threshold. Read against an explicit **hypothesis space** — every answer key still considered possible — a reply is a measurement, not a score. `mva.pipeline.probe_design` simulates the reply for every key with the local scorer replica, groups keys by the reply they produce (the **decode table**), and reports the expected information gain in bits. Two facts the designer surfaced, both under test: a single allele ranked *below* the pair adds almost nothing (it cannot say which member of the pair it partners), while an alternative **pair** row at rank *r* decodes directly through `full_match_rank = r` and earns 50 or 25 points instead of 10. So ranks 2–5 hold pairs. | rank | epcr | type | row | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | 0.9963 | primary | **BUB1B stop_gained + missense** (H009) | | 2–3 | 0.0014 · 0.0014 | primary | stop + the gnomAD-absent intronic BUB1B allele; stop + the rare intronic allele (ClinVar VUS) | | 4–5 | 0.00048 · 0.00041 | primary | missense + the gnomAD-absent intronic allele; missense + the rare intronic allele | | 6 | 0.00021 | secondary | **LZTR1** heterozygous stop_gained, ClinVar P/LP — dominant schwannomatosis predisposition, unrelated to MVA | | 7 | 0.00001 | secondary | **FLG** heterozygous stop_gained, ClinVar P — ichthyosis vulgaris / atopy | | 8 | 0.000006 | secondary | **F5** Factor V Leiden, heterozygous — low-penetrance thrombosis risk | **No number in this table was typed.** The rank-1 epcr is the register's suggested confidence for H009 (a transparent triage heuristic, not a calibrated posterior — §8). Every other primary row takes a share of the remaining mass in proportion to its pair score (rarity × severity per allele, `mva.pipeline.ranking`, summed), secondary rows sit below the lowest primary ordered by allele score, and the notes the organisers receive quote only columns of the warehouse result table each allele was selected from. The arithmetic, line by line, is [`derivation.md`](derivation.md); the tool refuses a hand-typed epcr, a note, a number inside a rationale, or an anchor row the ranker would not itself put first ([082](../../../docs/iteration1/step-6/methodology/082-derived-submission-rows.md)). ![What each possible reply would tell us](../../../figures/track1/track1-decode-table.png) > **Legend** — **green = the pair confirmed at rank 1**; **yellow = a reply that needs a > follow-up probe**; **red = nothing matched**; **blue = a decisive alternative**. Rehearsed byte-for-byte on the replica **and re-graded with the organisers' published `evaluation.py`** — the two scorers agree on every one of the eight keys ([075](../../../docs/step-0/methodology/075-coordinate-gate-and-redaction.md)). If the pair is right, **100 points, F-max 1.0**. Seven distinguishable replies over eight keys; prior entropy 1.11 bits, **expected gain 0.96 bits** (the derived priors put 0.78 of the mass on the anchor pair, so there is less to learn than the hand-set priors of entry 074 pretended). The one residual ambiguity is structural — "one allele right, partner not in the callset" cannot say *which* allele — and it is the exact trigger for the raw-read route (step 5) and a two-row singles probe. Rows 6–8 are secondary findings: free under the scoring rules (rows below the hit cannot lower F-max), reviewed qualitatively, chosen by a stated rule (ClinVar P/LP after excluding conflicts and benign-tagged records, gnomAD < 0.02, dominant or risk-factor genes; recessive carrier states GNRHR, CIAO1, ZFYVE26 are reported here, not submitted). **Not uploaded.** The four gate conditions of [step 6](../../../docs/iteration1/step-6/README.md) hold — normalized spellings, hypotheses with predictions and refutations, a byte-level rehearsal, four agreeing methods — and the timing is the team's decision. File: `submissions/track1/iteration-1/agharsallah_bub1b-comphet-derived.csv` (in the iteration folder, gitignored; sha256 `54854a6e…`; the filename carries the username and the approach, as the submission page asks). --- ## 8. Reproducibility, runtime and cost ```bash uv sync --all-groups uv run python tools/build_coding_regions.py --gtf Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.116.gtf.gz # 5 s uv run mva-warehouse stage && uv run mva-warehouse pg-ingest --tables coding_regions # 23 s uv run mva-warehouse pg-derive --only coding_alleles # ~17 min (WAN pull of 5 M rows) uv run mva-warehouse annotate-coding --workers 4 # ~33 min, resumable uv run mva-warehouse pg-derive --only coding_candidates gene_biallelic # 24 s uv run python tools/render_track1_figures.py uv run python tools/resolve_submission_spec.py --selectors submissions/track1/iteration-1/spec.selectors.json --out build/submission/spec.json # selectors → coordinates uv run python tools/design_submission.py --spec build/submission/spec.json --out submissions/track1/iteration-1/agharsallah_bub1b-comphet-derived.csv # CSV + rehearsal + cross-check ``` The submission itself is reproducible without a single committed coordinate: every allele in `spec.selectors.json` is a *selector* (gene, consequence, ClinVar and gnomAD flags) that must match exactly one row of the warehouse; the resolver refuses anything else. Everything ran on one laptop against a small hosted PostgreSQL and the free Ensembl REST API: **about one hour of wall clock, no paid compute**. The heavy alternative — aligning 160 Gb of reads — was not needed for the answer and stays conditional. [`tools/check-python.sh`](../../../tools/check-python.sh) runs the eight quality gates (the last two are the coordinate gate and the iteration-folder gate); the new tooling adds 77 tests across eight new test modules, 1,687 in all. --- ## 9. Limitations, stated - **Coding-only scope.** The genome-wide scan covers CDS ± 8 bp (1.4 % of the genome). A deep-intronic, UTR or structural second allele in *another* gene is outside it. Within BUB1B the two only rare non-coding alleles were checked (SpliceAI 0.00). - **Phase unresolved.** No reads or parents connect the two alleles; trans is inferred. - **No mosaicism measurement.** Bulk blood WGS bounds the aneuploid fraction below ≈ 10–15 %; it does not measure it. - **Missing feature.** Microcephaly, usual in MVA1, is not among the delivered terms. - **Confidence numbers are a heuristic.** The register's weighing is transparent arithmetic for triage, not a calibrated posterior; evidence rows about the same two alleles are not independent, which is why H009 carries no committed confidence. - **The oracle is the only authority.** The scorer replica is transcribed from the published code, tested against hand-derived values, and cross-checked key by key against the organisers' own `evaluation.py`; agreement between two scorers proves the *grading* is right, nothing about the answer key. --- ## 10. Methods form (Track 1), answered | Question | Answer | |---|---| | Model | one approach, model 1: panel filter → genome-wide coding scan → phenotype join → pair submission | | Automated or curated? | **Automated** to the ranked gene table and the candidate pair; the submission *layout* (which alternative pairings and secondary rows fill ranks 2–8) is a designed measurement, chosen by a stated rule and simulated, not hand-curated from belief | | Public data only? | **Yes**: Ensembl 116 gene models and VEP (gnomAD v4, ClinVar, SpliceAI, AlphaMissense, CADD), HPO release 2026-06-23, PubMed. No proprietary data | | Pairs or singles? | **Pairs**: every primary row is a compound-heterozygous pair in one row; the pipeline ranks pairs, not variants | | Secondary findings | ClinVar P/LP after excluding conflicting and benign-tagged records, gnomAD AF < 0.02, dominant or risk-factor genes → three rows marked `secondary`; recessive carrier states reported, not submitted | | Runtime and cost | ~1 h wall clock on one laptop, free public APIs, one small hosted PostgreSQL; no paid compute | | Abstract | §1 and §9 above, 300 words together | --- ## 11. ALT is matched by list membership — variants_raw keeps a multi-allelic site comma-packed (G -> A,C in one row) while the annotations are one row per ALT, so the join tests that the annotated allele is an element of the split list rather than a substring of the packed string, which would match A against AT. GT and DP are located by reading the record's own FORMAT keys, never by position.

Non-PASS alleles are counted separately so a gene one suppressed call short of biallelic is visible rather than dropped.

register.statement: The gene carrying the causal compound-heterozygous pair ranks in the top 30 of a phenotype-driven ranking that never reads the callset, the candidate panel, or any variant.
The parental term HP:0200067 (recurrent spontaneous abortion) degrades the phenotype ranking of the causal gene and should be excluded from the proband's term set.

retrospective: filtering the annotated eight-gene MVA panel to alleles that are both rare (gnomAD AF absent or below the recessive cutoff) and protein-altering (VEP impact HIGH or MODERATE) leaves exactly one candidate biallelic set, and it is in BUB1B: one stop_gained allele (ClinVar pathogenic) and one missense allele (absent from gnomAD), both heterozygous, both PASS.

No protein-coding gene outside the eight-gene panel carries a candidate biallelic set of rare protein-altering PASS alleles that outranks the BUB1B pair: BUB1B is the only gene that is biallelic on PASS calls AND carries a ClinVar pathogenic allele AND sits in the top 30 of the panel-blind phenotype ranking.

Among all genes that carry a candidate biallelic set of rare protein-altering PASS alleles genome-wide, BUB1B is the best-ranked gene in the panel-blind phenotype ranking — the two independent signals (DNA-derived biallelic set, symptom-derived gene rank) converge on one gene.

retrospective: none of the non-PASS calls inside the eight-gene panel is a credible hidden second allele — after VEP annotation, zero are both rare and protein-altering; TRIP13's cluster of filtered calls is a paralogous-read pileup (low allele fraction, all gnomAD-common).

Genome-wide, no gene reaches a biallelic set only by rescuing a suppressed (non-PASS) coding call while also carrying a ClinVar pathogenic or LoF allele and a top-30 phenotype rank; in particular BUB1B carries no rare protein-altering non-PASS coding allele, so the BUB1B pair does not depend on a filter rescue and no rescued call adds a third BUB1B candidate.

Both BUB1B candidate alleles are single-nucleotide substitutions at bi-allelic sites, so their submission spelling (chromosome, position, REF, ALT) is invariant under bcftools norm (left-alignment and multi-allelic splitting) and an exact-string scorer will match them as the callset spells them.
The causal compound-heterozygous pair is the BUB1B stop_gained allele (ClinVar pathogenic for MVA syndrome 1) together with the BUB1B missense allele absent from gnomAD, in trans.

Model 2 is the blind mirror of model 1: it rebuilds the answer from the raw reads, the VCF and the eight HPO terms with no candidate allele, gene or iteration-1 table allowed as an input until a final comparison step (a CI gate, tools/check_blind.py, enforces the declared inputs of every methodology entry). Six research steps, each with pre-registered hypotheses: (1) a symptom-only gene ranking (Exomiser's human-phenotype path re-implemented over HPO release 2026-06-23) produces a 404-gene target set in three tiers plus 396 length-matched decoy genes; its held-out recall@300 is measured on all 3,240 recessive diseases (0.335), so the set is treated as an enrichment, never as coverage. (2) A reference k-mer bait (every 31-mer of the 792 target and decoy genes, 2-bit packed, binary search behind a bitmap) selects from 1.07 billion reads the 14.7 million that touch those genes in one 50.8-minute server pass; minimap2 alignment; two small-variant callers with disjoint models (freebayes, bcftools call -m) and two structural-variant method classes (delly, dysgu); WhatsHap phasing; per-exon depth. Concordance with the vendor's genotypes is 0.9957 and 0.9927; 1,199 coding-adjacent alleles the vendor never reported are annotated. (3) An alignment-free, caller-free genotyper counts allele-specific k-mer pairs (381,510 probe pairs, 164,044 alleles) under a negative-binomial model fitted on 20,000 calibration markers, and a k-mer copy-number pass measures every target exon against a decoy null band. (4) A genome-wide likelihood-ratio ranking over every coding allele in the VCF with no hard filter: one calibrated lane per consequence class on the Tavtigian ACMG ladder (LOFTEE-style truncation rules, AlphaMissense, SpliceAI, ClinVar, gnomAD frequency, a non-PASS down-weight), a phenotype lane calibrated on step 1's own measured recall curve, and a STRING network lane for uncurated genes; 51,920 biallelic pair hypotheses over 11,465 genes, with two nulls (1,000-draw permutation of matched term sets; matched decoys through the same ratio) and a genotype-only ablation. (5) A knowledge engine over 815 genes (LitVar published alleles, PubTator gene-by-term co-mentions, UniProt/InterPro/AlphaFold domain and confidence for each missense) judged against a PubMed hit-count baseline and matched decoys. (6) Reciprocal rank fusion (k = 60, fixed) of the routes that pass an admission rule (separates targets from decoys and reorders a trivial baseline); the read route confirms at weight 0; the ranking is hashed before the comparison, then a separate tool reads the pair to look for from iteration 1's committed selector file. Step 8 bounds mosaic aneuploidy per chromosome with two instruments sharing nothing past the FASTQ. Full report and code: https://github.com/agharsallah/mva-hackathon (submissions/track1/iteration-2/).

Automated. The fused ranking and its rank-1 pair were produced and hashed (sha256 recorded in methodology entry 108) before any comparison with iteration 1 or with the confirmed answer. The submission file is built from coordinate-free selectors by tools: the rank-1 epcr is the register's suggested confidence for the anchor hypothesis, secondary rows sit below it by allele score, notes quote only columns of the warehouse table each allele was selected from, and the tool refuses a typed epcr, a typed note, or a digit inside a rationale. The submission layout (one primary pair, three secondary rows) follows a stated rule and was simulated against the scorer replica and the organisers' evaluation.py.

None on the candidate. Manual choices, all fixed before the runs and recorded in docs/iteration2/plan.md: the target-set cutoff (N = 300) and tiers; the fusion constant (k = 60) and the route-admission rule; the ACMG ladder values and the pre-registered cap of the AlphaMissense and SpliceAI lanes at 'moderate' (the mapping papers could not be fetched; the report names this the most load-bearing assumption); the secondary-finding rule (ClinVar P/LP after excluding conflicting and benign-tagged records, gnomAD AF < 0.02, dominant or risk-factor genes). Two planned instruments were cut and recorded (ESM1b, an LLM evidence tournament); four named tools had no arm64 build and were substituted with a recorded reason. LLM assistance (Anthropic API, Claude) was used to write code and documentation; no LLM judged a variant.
Public data only.

GRCh38 no-alt + hs38d1 reference (195 contigs) for the bait, probes and alignment; Ensembl release 116 gene models (GTF, coding regions) and VEP REST with gnomAD v4 frequencies, ClinVar classifications, AlphaMissense and SpliceAI; ClinVar GRCh38 VCF for the pathogenic/likely-pathogenic allele catalogue typed in step 3; gnomAD v2 co-occurrence for P(trans) (GRCh37, bridged by dbSNP id); HPO release 2026-06-23 (hp.obo, genes_to_phenotype); Phen2Gene and Monarch semsim REST as a second phenotype ranker; STRING v12 interaction partners (score >= 700); LitVar 2.0, PubTator 3.0, PubMed E-utilities; UniProt, InterPro, AlphaFold DB (per-residue pLDDT); UCSC cytobands for chromosome arms. Every reference build carries a provenance manifest (URL, release, SHA-256), and every derived table an edge in warehouse.data_lineage naming the delivered callset object and the clinical document by digest.
None.

Pairs. Step 4 enumerates biallelic hypotheses per gene (compound heterozygous pairs, homozygous alleles, and single alleles as a separate shape) and ranks the pair, not the variant; step 6 fuses at the pair level; the primary row holds both alleles (chrom_1/pos_1 + chrom_2/pos_2). The pair's phase could not be measured by the reads (no phase block reaches it) nor by population co-occurrence (undetermined); the trans configuration rests on the recessive model and on the oracle's reply to submission 1, and the report says so.

Three rows are marked finding_type=secondary, below the primary hit so they cannot lower F-max: a heterozygous LZTR1 stop_gained (ClinVar P/LP; dominant schwannomatosis predisposition, unrelated to MVA), a heterozygous FLG stop_gained (ClinVar P; ichthyosis vulgaris / atopy) and Factor V Leiden (F5, heterozygous, low-penetrance thrombosis risk factor). Rule: ClinVar pathogenic/likely pathogenic after excluding conflicting and benign-tagged records, gnomAD AF < 0.02, dominant or risk-factor genes; recessive carrier states are reported in iteration 1's report, not submitted. Iteration 2 also typed 88,754 ClinVar P/LP alleles alignment-free in the raw reads: 15 are present at heterozygous multiplicity across 14 genes, one of them the BUB1B stop; the others are listed in methodology entry 103 and were not promoted to rows, because four of the five confident ClinVar calls in target genes are an artefact of an over-tight fitted error rate (entry 096).

Two read passes ran on a small Linux server holding the 272-shard read store: the bait sweep over 1,071,835,104 reads in 50.8 minutes (4.2 hours projected on the laptop), and the k-mer dosage tally over 32 of 272 shards (124.5 million reads) in 2,803.8 seconds. Everything else ran on one arm64 laptop (16 GiB): bait build 51 s; k-mer genotype counting 765 s and copy-number counting 512 s over the baited reads; the 1,000-draw permutation null 34 minutes; the 3,240-disease phenotype benchmark about 2 h 16 min on one core; 5,705 PubTator searches and the LitVar/UniProt/InterPro/AlphaFold fetches against free public APIs; the fusion, unblinding, submission build and figure rendering in minutes. Storage: a hosted PostgreSQL (about 1.5 GB) and an object store for the reads. Cost: no paid compute; a small hosted database (about 5 euro per month).

We rebuilt, blind, the causal compound-heterozygous pair for a child with mosaic variegated aneuploidy (MVA), a chromosome-instability disorder, after the challenge scorer had confirmed iteration 1's answer (BUB1B stop_gained + BUB1B missense) with a full match at rank 1. The question: was the pipeline right, or lucky? Iteration 2 started from the raw reads, the VCF and the eight HPO terms with no iteration-1 candidate or table allowed as input until a final comparison, enforced by a CI gate over every methodology entry's declared inputs. Six pre-registered research steps: a symptom-only target set whose held-out recall@300 was measured (0.335, not the 0.90 predicted) so it is an enrichment, not coverage; a reference k-mer read bait recovering 14.7 M of 1.07 B reads in one 50.8-minute pass, two independent callers reproducing the vendor's genotypes at 99.57 % and 99.27 % and reporting 1,199 alleles the vendor never did; an alignment-free, caller-free k-mer genotyper and copy-number pass typing 164,044 alleles, which finds both lead alleles at one copy each (posterior 1.0) and every BUB1B exon at two copies; a genome-wide likelihood-ratio ranking with no hard filter over 51,920 biallelic hypotheses in 11,465 genes, where the pair leads at ratio 341,019 (runner-up 1.70x behind and phased cis) and targets separate from matched decoys at AUC 0.706 [0.655, 0.751]; a knowledge engine over 815 genes, measured weak (AUC 0.634, gene rank 293 of 815); and a reciprocal-rank fusion frozen by hash before unblinding. The same two alleles came out first under both weightings. Strengths: replication by disjoint instruments, each with a measured error rate; every claim filed before its test with a refutation condition (40 hypotheses across steps 1-6 and 8, 16 refuted and reported); matched decoy nulls throughout; case-agnostic tools (k-mer bait and counting kernel, negative-binomial k-mer genotyper, calibrated LR pair ranker, RRF fuser with leave-one-out and freeze receipt, blind gate); coordinate-free selectors, so the submission rebuilds anywhere without a committed position. A second instrument bounds the disease's defining feature: no chromosome in the sequenced sample carries a mosaic aneuploidy above 2-3 % of cells (allele balance, 80 % power on 24 of 24 contigs, where the earlier statistic had power on none) or 1.6 % (k-mer dosage, X and Y recovered at one copy as the control). Limitations: one route carried the rediscovery (silencing the likelihood ranker drops the pair to rank 62; the symptom route had it at 9; the literature never listed it); the rank-1 position depends on the clinical terms and on one calibration cap; phase is unmeasured by reads or population data and rests on the oracle's reply; the read route has no ranking power of its own (targets and decoys equal, p = 0.589); four planned tools had no arm64 build; the mosaic bound concerns the sequenced sample only, with focal events invisible by construction. A second upload gains 0.000 bits on every expressible question, so this file is built and rehearsed on two scorers but held in reserve; 5 of 6 uploads remain.

# Track 1 report, iteration 2 — the same pair, found again with the answer hidden **Standing:** the Track-1 replication report, written 2026-09-19 from executed runs. Every number below was produced by the methodology entry cited beside it (`docs/iteration2/step-/methodology/`), and every claim is a pre-registered hypothesis in the append-only register ([`science-register.json`](../../../docs/science-register.json), rendered at [`figures/science-report.html`](../../../figures/science-report.html)). Submission 1 was uploaded on 2026-09-09 and answered *full match at rank 1, 100 rank points, F-max 1.0* ([083](../../../docs/iteration1/step-6/methodology/083-oracle-reply-submission-1.md)). **Submission 2 is built, rehearsed on two scorers and not uploaded**: it would teach nothing ([124](../../../docs/iteration2/step-6/methodology/124-the-reserve-file-built-and-rehearsed.md)), so 5 of 6 uploads stay in reserve. Written for a reader who knows software, not genetics. Each domain term is given as `technical term (plain meaning)` on first use; the full vocabulary is [`dictionary.md`](../../../docs/dictionary.md), served at `/learn` on the dashboard. --- ## 1. The answer in one paragraph The child has **mosaic variegated aneuploidy (MVA)**: some of his cells carry the wrong number of chromosomes, because the checkpoint that holds a dividing cell until every chromosome is attached is weak. Iteration 1 found the cause top-down, from the vendor's variant calls: two different broken copies of **BUB1B**, the gene for that checkpoint's protein BubR1, one copy from each parent (a **compound heterozygote**) — a **stop-gain** allele (a premature full stop, already classified pathogenic for MVA syndrome 1) and a **missense** allele (one amino acid swapped) that no population database has seen. The challenge's answer key confirmed that pair at rank 1. Iteration 2 asked a harder question: **would we have found it without knowing it?** It started again from the raw reads, the callset and the eight clinical terms, under a **blind protocol** (no iteration-1 candidate, gene or table allowed as an input), by routes that share no code with iteration 1 — a symptom-only gene ranking, a k-mer read bait with two independent callers, an alignment-free genotyper, a genome-wide likelihood-ratio ranking with no hard filter, and a public-knowledge engine — fused them, froze the ranking, and only then looked. **The same two BUB1B alleles came out first, under both weightings** ([109](../../../docs/iteration2/step-6/methodology/109-what-the-mirror-found.md)). The honest second half: one route found it, two corroborated it at a distance, one instrument confirmed it in the raw reads, and the literature never listed it. A second instrument then set the first real bound on the disease's defining feature: no chromosome in the sequenced sample carries a mosaic aneuploidy above 2–3 % of cells, where the earlier statistic had no power at all ([116](../../../docs/iteration2/step-8/methodology/116-the-statistic-that-has-power-and-the-limit-it-buys.md)). ```mermaid flowchart LR H[/"8 HPO terms"/]:::raw R[/"1.07 B raw reads

What the reply said, and what iteration 2 is for The scorer's reply to submission 1 — `full_match_rank 1`, `rank_points 100`, `f_max 1.0` at threshold 0.9963 — matched row 1 of iteration 1's pre-registered **decode table** (the lookup, built before the upload, that translates every possible reply into "which rows held the true alleles"). Survivors: `stop+missense` only. The seven alternative answer keys were eliminated in one upload; hypothesis H009 went to `supported` ([083](../../../docs/iteration1/step-6/methodology/083-oracle-reply-submission-1.md)). Nothing is left to *find* for the automated score. What is left is the question the automated score cannot ask: **is the pipeline right, or was it lucky?** Iteration 1 trusted the vendor's caller, applied hard filters (rarity, consequence) and checked that four instruments agreed. Each of those choices could have been the reason the pair surfaced. So iteration 2 is iteration 1's **mirror**, run **blind** ([plan §1](../../../docs/iteration2/plan.md)): | Allowed as input | Not allowed until step 6 | |---|---| | the 8 HPO terms; the FASTQ; the VCF; public knowledge (HPO, Ensembl, gnomAD, ClinVar, PubMed, protein models) | the identity of the two iteration-1 alleles; the gene name as a filter; iteration 1's decode table, verdicts and figures | | the step-0 platform (read store, warehouse, annotator, register, scorer replica) | any `results.*` table iteration 1 derived that encodes the candidate — iteration 2 re-derives its own under `results.it2_*` | The gene is written all over this repository, so the blinding is a **procedural rule, not a secret**: every methodology entry declares its inputs, and `tools/check_blind.py` (a CI gate) refuses an entry that names an iteration-1 candidate table before entry 109. Software analogy: not a sandbox, but a code review that rejects a forbidden import. The gate's current state: *38 iteration-2 entries, every one declaring its inputs — unblinded by 109*. A pair rediscovered from scratch by a disjoint route is the strongest replication a single sample allows, and it is what makes the tooling transferable to a case with **no answer key**. --- ## 3. The clinical picture, and how both inputs were used The challenge delivered eight **HPO terms** (Human Phenotype Ontology — a controlled vocabulary of clinical features, each with an id) and no karyotype: | Feature | HPO id | Where iteration 2 used it | |---|---|---| | Rhabdomyosarcoma (a childhood muscle-tissue cancer) | HP:0002859 | step 1 ranking; step 5 case-report search; Track 2 direction D4 | | Nephrocalcinosis | HP:0000121 | step 1; step 5 | | Short stature | HP:0004322 | step 1; step 5 | | Failure to thrive | HP:0001508 | step 1; step 5 | | Skeletal muscle atrophy | HP:0003202 | step 1; step 5 | | Premature birth | HP:0001622 | step 1; step 5 | | Small for gestational age | HP:0001518 | step 1; step 5 | | Recurrent spontaneous abortion (**parental** history) | HP:0200067 | step 1's `with-parental` query only; the recessive-with-lethality prior in step 4 | Every step states which input it read. Step 1 read the clinical terms and **no DNA**. Steps 2 and 3 read the raw reads over a gene set that exists only because of the clinical terms. Step 4 read the VCF and the terms together, and its ablation says exactly what the terms added (§4.4). Step 5 read public knowledge against the seven proband terms. Step 8 read both raw inputs and the clinical document, and found in it no karyotype and no term a blood aneuploid fraction would predict ([115](../../../docs/iteration2/step-8/methodology/115-the-callset-reduced-to-what-a-mosaic-model-needs.md)). The warehouse's `data_lineage` table carries an edge from every derived table to both the delivered callset object and the clinical document by digest, and the submission's own three edges were appended by the resolver ([124](../../../docs/iteration2/step-6/methodology/124-the-reserve-file-built-and-rehearsed.md)). --- ## 4. The mirror, step by step Each step declared one goal in `src/mva/science/steps.py`, filed its hypotheses with a prediction and a refutation condition **before** running, and closed only when every hypothesis had a verdict. Refutations are reported with the same weight as supports: they are the half that changed the plan. ### 4.1 Step 1 — which genes do the symptoms alone nominate? a hosted PostgreSQL for the warehouse; free public APIs (Ensembl VEP REST, LitVar, PubTator, UniProt, InterPro, AlphaFold DB, PubMed, STRING). **No paid compute.** The k-mer engine's cost is bound by bytes of sequence, not by bait size (1.05× per read across 36,000× of bait), which is what makes "give me the reads for these genes" a case-agnostic tool. The tooling is generic: a reference k-mer read bait and counting kernel (`mva.kmer`), a negative-binomial k-mer genotyper and local-flank copy number, a per-lane calibrated likelihood-ratio pair ranker, a reciprocal-rank fuser with leave-one-out and a freeze receipt, a knowledge fetcher with matched-decoy baselines, a mosaic-fraction bound with two instruments and an injection harness, a blind gate, and a per-iteration step map. Every table is in `warehouse.data_lineage`; every figure is drawn from a run's own output file. `tools/check-python.sh` runs the eight quality gates, including the coordinate gate and the iteration-folder gate. --- ## 9. Limitations, stated - **One route carried the rediscovery.** Silence the likelihood ranker and the pair falls to rank 62; the symptom route had it at rank 9; the literature never listed it. "Three routes agree" would be false; "one found it, two corroborated it at a distance, one confirmed it in the reads" is the sentence ([109](../../../docs/iteration2/step-6/methodology/109-what-the-mirror-found.md)). - **The rank-1 position depends on the clinical terms and on one calibration cap.** DNA alone puts the pair joint third; capping the missense and splice lanes at *supporting* instead of *moderate* flips the lead to `ADAMTS1` ([099](../../../docs/iteration2/step-4/methodology/099-every-gene-ordered-with-nothing-filtered-out.md), [100](../../../docs/iteration2/step-4/methodology/100-two-nulls-and-an-ablation.md)). - **Phase is unmeasured.** No read-backed phase block reaches the pair and population co-occurrence is undetermined. *Trans* rests on the recessive model and on the oracle's answer key; iteration 2's own instruments cannot reach it. - **A rediscovery is not coverage.** The symptom ranker's held-out recall@300 is 0.335, and 73.6 % of protein-coding genes have no HPO curation; the route found *this* pair and says nothing about the next case. The genome-wide ranking is the safety net, and its permutation p is 0.056, not < 0.001. - **The read route has no ranking power of its own** (H020 refuted); its 1,199 novel alleles are corroborated at 35.3 % by the alignment-free instrument and are an upper bound with a measured error rate. Concordance with the vendor covers substitutions only; the structural variant consensus used two of four planned callers and no positive-control sample. - **Below rank 1 the fused ranking has poor resolution.** Rank inheritance makes the top 20 three genes; a matched decoy holds ranks 13–20. The confirmation triple is gene-level, not allele-level. - **The literature route is weak by measurement**, AUC 0.634, and would not have found the gene (rank 293 of 815). A publication is not evidence about this child; 95.1 % of alleles have one. - **The mosaic bound is about the sequenced sample.** Tissue unstated; focal and sub-arm events invisible by construction; copy-neutral loss of heterozygosity invisible to the dosage route; the mechanism-of-origin models do not fit this data at all. The dosage route's divisors were checked against each other (0.017 %) but were not put through the injection harness the allele route was ([118](../../../docs/iteration2/step-8/methodology/118-the-baseline-and-what-a-variegated-genome-does-to-it.md), [123](../../../docs/iteration2/step-8/methodology/123-the-denominator-that-assumes-nothing-read-back.md)). - **Confidence numbers are a heuristic.** The register's weighing is transparent arithmetic for triage, not a calibrated posterior; the epcr of 0.9993 inherits that caveat. - **Some of the plan's instruments never ran on this hardware**, and two exhibits (the per-exon depth grid, the BUB1B phase track) are committed figures not yet on the dashboard route (`docs/iteration2/step-2/notes/completion-audit.md`, D7–D8). --- ## 10. methods_form.answer: agharsallah

From variant to mechanism to medicine in four documented stages, each a case-agnostic tool with a provenance manifest. (1) Hand-off: Track 1's confirmed compound-heterozygous BUB1B pair (a stop allele + a kinase-region missense, trans configuration confirmed by the challenge's answer key) was written into a structured 'mechanism card' (ressources/track2/mechanism.json): gene, protein, the two allele classes (never positions), loss-of-function reading, the spindle-assembly-checkpoint pathway, downstream consequences, the tumour context (rhabdomyosarcoma) from the clinical terms, and four repurposing directions with seed genes - D1 reinforce the checkpoint, D2 exploit aneuploidy stress, D3 stabilise the remaining BubR1 (hypomorph), D4 the child's tumour. Iteration 2's measured genotype facts (allele dosage from the raw reads, exon copy number, structural-variant absence, the missense's position in the protein, pathogenicity lanes, P(trans)) were appended as a card revision (v3), with the aneuploidy burden marked unmeasured. (2) Search: the card's seeds were expanded through Reactome pathways to 277 targets; Open Targets, ChEMBL and DGIdb returned 3,859 drug-target rows and 359 market-approved drugs; openFDA confirmed US labels; ClinicalTrials.gov and PubMed answered trial and literature questions, all queries derived from the card. (3) Grading: every approved drug on every direction was placed on a five-rung evidence ladder pre-registered before the search (5 approved for a related indication with paediatric use; 4 trial in a related indication; 3 animal model of the mechanism; 2 cell model; 1 mechanism only - named, never submitted). Automated tests (approval, label and its Pediatric Use section, tumour-context trials, studies admitting children, PubMed co-mention counts) and curated tests (one PubMed paper per row, read by a person, 13 rows) are printed side by side; inherited class-level evidence is marked 'proxy'. Six falsifiable claims (one per direction, one for the control, one for paediatric data) were registered with predictions and refutation conditions before any drug-level query. (4) Control: the same pipeline ran on two decoy cards - the child's clinical side kept, the gene swapped (NTRK3 by a seeded draw from Track 1's decoy set; XDH, an unrelated metabolic enzyme). This is a negative control in the usual sense: an input the pipeline should not be able to argue from, run through the unchanged code so that whatever comes out for the decoy as readily as for BUB1B is attributed to database density or the clinical queries rather than to the mechanism. A direction whose approved drugs overlap a decoy's at Jaccard >= 0.10 is reported as non-specific; D4 did (0.25) and is argued only from curated mechanism results. Output: 11 drugs with a cited mechanism result (statins; niacin/nicotinamide; chloroquine; bortezomib, metformin, valproic acid, vorinostat, hydroxychloroquine, atorvastatin), 50 drugs already in rhabdomyosarcoma trials listed as such, and a 23-drug do-not table (spindle poisons, checkpoint inhibitors, standard of care).

Both, kept apart and printed side by side. Automated: drug-target database queries (Open Targets, ChEMBL, DGIdb, Reactome, openFDA, ClinicalTrials.gov, PubMed E-utilities) driven by the mechanism card, plus per-drug PubMed co-mention counts and paediatric-trial lookups; these produce the candidate set and the automated rungs 4-5. Manual: the evidence rungs 2-3 come from 13 papers read by a person and entered in evidence.tsv with the PubMed id, the model (cell / in vivo) and a proxy flag when the paper tested a same-axis compound rather than the approved drug. LLM assistance was used to draft queries, code and prose; every PubMed id was resolved live against E-utilities before it was written down, and four ids first recalled from memory were wrong and replaced by title search before entering any file.

Thirteen curated rows, each one cited result: Tang & Amon 2011 (PMID 21315436) - chloroquine and the AMPK activator AICAR are aneuploidy-selective in trisomic and aneuploid cells (rung 2 for chloroquine; metformin and hydroxychloroquine inherit as proxies); Ippolito 2024 (39247952) and Chui 2019 (31530568) - aneuploid cells depend on protein degradation and are more sensitive to proteasome inhibition (bortezomib, class proxy); North 2014 (24825348) - the NAD+ precursor NMN raised BubR1 in vivo and SIRT2 extended the lifespan of BubR1-hypomorphic mice (rung 3; niacin and nicotinamide as proxies); Park 2017 (28985013) and Choi 2009 (19407811) - HDAC2/3 deacetylation drives BubR1 degradation, acetylation protects it (valproic acid, vorinostat as class proxies); Gizaw 2025 (41249736) - lovastatin itself reduced rhabdomyosarcoma cell proliferation and cholesterol synthesis is a non-redundant tumour vulnerability (rung 2; simvastatin and atorvastatin as proxies). The anti-directions rest on Suijkerbuijk 2010 (20516114, MVA cells have a weakened checkpoint), Sinha 2019 (30601084, mitotic slippage) and Cohen-Sharir 2021 (33505028, aneuploid cells are killed by checkpoint inhibition). The mechanism section rests on Hanks 2004 (15475955) and Suijkerbuijk 2010. Curation was one person's reading of the abstracts on 2026-09-18; every row carries its PubMed id so it can be checked.
Publicly available sources only. No proprietary data source was used.

Open Targets Platform (GraphQL API, drugAndClinicalCandidates per target and disease), ChEMBL (REST: target search, mechanism, molecule max_phase, first approval, ATC), DGIdb (GraphQL interactions), Reactome ContentService (pathways containing the protein, participants), openFDA drug labels (current US label; the pediatric_use section), ClinicalTrials.gov v2 (studies by condition and intervention; aggFilters=ages:child for studies admitting children), PubMed E-utilities (esearch counts and ids, esummary), plus ClinVar (the stop allele's classification) and gnomAD (population absence of the missense) from Track 1. DrugBank was named by the form but not queried: its programmatic access needs a licence. Every reply is cached and its digest rolled into the table's manifest; retrieval dates are 2026-09-05 (first snapshot) and 2026-09-18 (refresh and enrichment).
None.

Loss of function, hypomorphic, of a confirmed compound heterozygote. One allele is a stop change in exon 17 of 23 (ClinVar pathogenic / likely pathogenic for MVA syndrome 1): no functional BubR1 from that copy. The other is a missense change in the last exon: absent from gnomAD, AlphaMissense likely-pathogenic (log-likelihood-ratio lane 4.33), CADD 24.5, sitting outside every InterPro domain-typed entry in a region AlphaFold models at pLDDT 91 - a weakened copy, not a dead one, consistent with every published MVA1 genotype (complete loss is embryonic-lethal). No gain-of-function or dominant-negative activity is reported for BUB1B. Trans configuration: confirmed by the oracle's full match at rank 1 (population phasing was undetermined; read-backed phase blocks did not reach the gene). Dosage: both alleles at one-copy multiplicity in the raw reads by an alignment-free k-mer method; every exon at two copies; no structural variant in the gene. Pathway: the spindle assembly checkpoint - BubR1 is a core component of the mitotic checkpoint complex that inhibits APC/C-CDC20 and recruits PP2A-B56 to kinetochores; less BubR1 gives a leaky checkpoint (Suijkerbuijk 2010 measured strongly reduced BubR1 and a weakened checkpoint in MVA cells). Downstream: premature anaphase and chromosome missegregation; mosaic variegated aneuploidy; proteotoxic and metabolic stress in aneuploid cells; cancer predisposition (rhabdomyosarcoma - the child's presenting tumour - Wilms tumour, leukaemia); growth restriction and nephrocalcinosis, which are the delivered clinical terms. Stated gaps: the aneuploid fraction in this child's sample is unmeasured (the karyotype statistic run had no power for mosaic gains; the powered analysis is planned), and whether the missense copy is unstable or catalytically inactive is open - so direction D3 is argued as raising BubR1 abundance, not as refolding it.

Roughly four working days across two people-equivalents: one day for the mechanism card and the data layer (iteration 1, 2026-09-05/06), and about three days on 2026-09-18 for the card revision, the six pre-registered claims, the enrichment adapters and ladder, the decoy control, the curation, the figures, the dashboard page and this report. Compute and cost: a laptop, two runs of about ten minutes each (the snapshot and the enrichment) against seven public APIs, most of that runtime spent waiting politely between per-drug requests rather than computing; seconds on a re-run once the replies are cached. No cloud, no GPU, no cluster, no paid data source and no licence fee - the only cost that does not shrink on a second case is the person-read curation (13 abstracts, one reader, one day).

Question. Given a confirmed compound-heterozygous loss of BUB1B (a stop allele and a hypomorphic kinase-region missense) in a child with mosaic variegated aneuploidy and rhabdomyosarcoma, which market-approved drugs act on the mechanism, and how strong is the evidence for each? Method. A structured mechanism card written from Track 1's confirmed result and iteration 2's measured genotype facts drives every query: Reactome expands the card's seed genes to 277 targets; Open Targets, ChEMBL and DGIdb return 359 approved drugs; openFDA, ClinicalTrials.gov and PubMed answer label, trial and literature questions per drug. Every approved drug on every direction is placed on a five-rung evidence ladder pre-registered before the search (approved with paediatric use; trial in a related indication; animal model; cell model; mechanism only), with the automated tests and the 13 person-curated PubMed rows printed side by side and inherited class-level evidence flagged as proxy. Six claims were registered with refutation conditions before any drug-level query. The whole pipeline ran unchanged on two decoy cards (same child, gene swapped for NTRK3 and for XDH) as a specificity control. Results. Direction D1 (reinforce the checkpoint) has no approved drug and became the do-not table. D2 (aneuploidy stress): chloroquine has a molecule-level cell result; metformin, hydroxychloroquine and bortezomib inherit class-level results. D3 (raise BubR1): NAD+ repletion raised BubR1 in BubR1-hypomorphic mice, inherited by niacin and nicotinamide (rung 3); HDAC inhibitors act on BubR1's acetylation switch at class level. D4 (the tumour): lovastatin itself slowed rhabdomyosarcoma cells, and a completed paediatric phase-1 trial gave simvastatin with chemotherapy in relapsed solid tumours including rhabdomyosarcoma. Eleven drugs carry a cited mechanism result; fifty more reach the top rung only because they are already in rhabdomyosarcoma trials and are listed as such, not claimed. The decoy control showed D4's automated stage is non-specific (Jaccard 0.25 against NTRK3) while D1-D3 are gene-specific, and it exposed a grading flaw (tumour trials lifting mechanism directions) that was corrected before any verdict, with the change recorded. The do-not table names 13 spindle poisons - including standard rhabdomyosarcoma chemotherapy - as a caution for the treating team, because those drugs rely on the very checkpoint that is weakened, and no approved checkpoint inhibitor exists. Strengths. Pre-registration; a decoy control for a repurposing pipeline; automated and curated evidence never merged silently; complete lineage (manifests, warehouse edges); case-agnostic tooling (swap the card, run another case); no patient data in any Track 2 artifact. Limitations. Curated rungs are one reader's; rung 3 is a single mouse paper; the child's aneuploid fraction is unmeasured; the missense's unstable-versus-inactive status is open; DrugBank was not queried; a paediatric pointer is not safety data. These are hypotheses for follow-up, not evidence that any medicine works.

report.markdown:
# Track 2 report — which approved medicines could act on this child's broken checkpoint? **Standing:** draft, written 2026-09-18 from executed runs (iteration 2, step 7 — methodology entries [110](../../../docs/iteration2/step-7/methodology/110-the-card-revised-and-the-claims-filed-before-the-search.md)–[113](../../../docs/iteration2/step-7/methodology/113-the-ladder-the-shortlist-and-the-do-not-table.md)). Every number is read from a table with a provenance manifest, every claim was registered before its test, and every cited paper was resolved against PubMed the same day. **Superseded by [`../iteration-2/`](../iteration-2/report.md) and never uploaded** — kept for provenance, with its facts frozen at mechanism card **version 3** (the aneuploidy burden, fact F8, is *unmeasured* here). Restructured on 2026-09-20 to the same four-criteria shape as iteration 2, **with every fact unchanged at card v3**: sections were added and renumbered, nothing was remeasured and no later result was imported. Written for the panel, in plain words. Each technical term appears once with its meaning in brackets; the full dictionary is served at `/learn` on the dashboard. > The challenge's own framing, kept in view throughout: *submissions are hypotheses for > follow-up, not evidence that a medicine works.* Nothing below is a recommendation to treat. --- ## 1. How this report answers the panel's four criteria > **Rubric:** all four — this section is the map, and the last column names each criterion's > weakest point before a judge has to go looking for it. | criterion | weight | where in this report | the evidence, in one line | the weakest point we know | |---|---|---|---|---| | **Scientific Rigor** | 35 % | §2, §4, §5, §6, §10, §12 | the mechanism is read off a genotype the challenge's answer key confirmed, with nine facts measured onto the card; every approved drug sits on a five-rung ladder written before the search; six claims were registered with their refutation conditions before any drug-level query | **no approved drug has a molecule-level result on BubR1 itself.** The deepest mechanism lead (D3) is one mouse paper, and the two approved molecules inherit it as a *proxy* | | **Potential Impact** | 25 % | §7, and the do-not table in §6.3 | a do-not table naming 13 spindle poisons — two of them this child's standard chemotherapy — that work by relying on the very checkpoint that is broken; the D1 result and that caution follow from the checkpoint, so they are arguments about the disease, not only about this gene | the child's **aneuploid fraction is unmeasured in this draft**, so direction D2 is argued from published aneuploid-cell biology and not from him; and nothing here is evidence that a medicine works | | **Innovation** | 25 % | §8, §5.3 | one structured mechanism card drives every query; the same pipeline is re-run on a decoy gene as a negative control and the overlap is measured against a threshold fixed in advance; automated and person-read evidence are printed side by side; the do-not table is a first-class output | these are **process** innovations, not new biology: no new model, no new algorithm, and knowledge-graph repurposing rankers already exist (§8) | | **Scalability** | 15 % | §9, §11 | one card in, five commands out, every table carrying its own provenance manifest; the whole run is two laptop runs of about ten minutes against public APIs, seconds when cached, no cloud | the curated rungs are the human bottleneck — 13 abstracts read by one person on one day — and the transfer run onto a genuinely different case **post-dates this draft** and belongs to iteration 2 (§9) | --- ## 2. The answer in one page > **Rubric:** Scientific Rigor — the whole claim on one page: the mechanism read off a > confirmed genotype, the four directions with the highest rung each reached, and what is > not known. Every later section exists to support or qualify something stated here. **The child.** A boy with mosaic variegated aneuploidy (MVA: in some of his cells, a chromosome is missing or duplicated, and different cells are wrong in different ways), short stature, failure to thrive, calcium deposits in the kidneys, and a rhabdomyosarcoma (a muscle-tissue cancer of childhood). Eight clinical terms were delivered with the case. **The cause.** Track 1 found, and the challenge's answer key confirmed, two different broken copies of one gene, `BUB1B` — one from each parent (a *compound heterozygote*). The gene makes BubR1, the protein that acts as the **brake** on cell division: it holds a dividing cell until every chromosome is properly attached before the cell is allowed to split. One copy makes no protein at all (a *stop* change); the other makes a weakened protein (a *missense* change in the protein's last stretch). The child therefore has **some brake, but less than normal** — which is exactly the pattern every published MVA case with this gene shows, because having no brake at all is not survivable. **The mechanism, in the form the methods form asks for.** *Loss of function*, not gain: less BubR1, a leakier checkpoint, chromosomes that separate too early, cells with the wrong count, and — in surviving cells — a chronic stress from carrying the wrong number of copies of many proteins. Downstream: the aneuploidy that names the disease, the growth problems, and a predisposition to exactly the cancers this child has. **Four ways a drug could act, graded on a ladder written before the search.** | Direction | The idea | What we found | Best rung | |---|---|---|---| | **D1** reinforce the brake | make the remaining checkpoint stronger | **no approved drug does this.** Every checkpoint drug on the market or in trials *weakens* it. D1 became the do-not table | — | | **D2** exploit the stress of aneuploid cells | aneuploid cells are already stressed; some approved drugs tip them over | **chloroquine** (a malaria drug) killed aneuploid cells preferentially in the reference screen; metformin, hydroxychloroquine and bortezomib inherit the result through their drug class | 2 (cell model) | | **D3** raise the amount of working BubR1 | the weakened copy still works; stabilise it | **niacin / nicotinamide** (vitamin B3 forms): boosting the NAD⁺ pathway raised BubR1 in mice bred to have too little of it; valproic acid and vorinostat act on BubR1's acetylation switch | 3 (animal model) | | **D4** the child's actual tumour | approved, non-chemotherapy drugs with a mechanism in rhabdomyosarcoma | **statins** (lovastatin, simvastatin, atorvastatin): rhabdomyosarcoma cells depend on making their own cholesterol; lovastatin itself slowed them; simvastatin has already been in a completed paediatric sarcoma trial | 5 (approved, trialled in this tumour, used in children) — carried by rung-2 mechanism evidence | **The half a clinician may care about most: what not to do.** Thirteen approved drugs are *spindle poisons* — they work by jamming cell division and relying on the checkpoint to hold the cell. In a child whose checkpoint is the broken part, that reliance is a hypothesis worth weighing before treatment. Several of them (vincristine, vinorelbine) are standard rhabdomyosarcoma chemotherapy. **This report flags the question for the treating team; it does not advise withholding standard care.** **What we do not know.** How aneuploid this child's cells actually are (the sequencing data delivered cannot measure it with any power; the analysis that could is planned and not run). Whether the weakened BubR1 copy is unstable or simply inactive. And whether any drug on this page helps — rung 3 is one mouse paper. --- ## 3. It was not run, and nothing in this report is evidence of what it would show.** ### 7.2 For others living with MVA: two results that belong to the mechanism, not to this gene MVA is not a one-gene disease, and its other known causes sit in the same chromosome-segregation machinery: `BUB1B` is the core of the checkpoint itself, `TRIP13` resets the MAD2 switch so the checkpoint signal can be rebuilt, and `CEP57` is part of the centrosome that builds the spindle the checkpoint watches. Whichever gene is broken, the cell ends up with **a leaky brake**. Two of this report's results are therefore arguments about a weakened checkpoint rather than about this child's particular gene: 1. **No approved drug reinforces the checkpoint** (direction D1, §2). Every marketed or trialled checkpoint drug is built to *weaken* it, because weakening it is what kills cancer cells. A child whose checkpoint is constitutionally weak is on the wrong side of that entire development programme — and that is true for any MVA genotype, not only this one. 2. **The spindle-poison caution** (§6.3). It rests on the checkpoint being leaky, which is the shared endpoint of every MVA gene above. Said plainly: this is reasoning *from* the mechanism, not a measurement across genes. The claim that the same pipeline reproduces both results on a different MVA gene is registered as **H066**, and its test **post-dates this draft** — see §9 and [`../iteration-2/report.md`](../iteration-2/report.md). ### 7.3 For diagnosis: a pipeline and its stated limits, not a measurement Be precise about what *this draft* contributes to recognising the condition.
