Could this run for the next child? > **Rubric:** Scalability — what it takes to point this pipeline at another person, another gene > or another disease, and what breaks first when you do. **Case-agnostic by construction.** The pipeline has one input — the mechanism card — and five commands (§11). Nothing about this child is compiled into a module: the gene, the allele classes, the pathway, the disease, the tumour context and the four directions are all fields on the card, and every table written out carries a provenance manifest naming its queries and its retrieval time. The decoy runs in §5.3 are the demonstration: the same code, one field changed, no edit. **The cost shape, measured on this case.** | resource | this case | |---|---| | compute | a laptop. Two runs of about ten minutes each — the snapshot and the enrichment — most of it polite waiting between requests; **seconds when the replies are cached**. No cloud, no GPU, no cluster | | data | seven public APIs; no licence, no patient-scale file to move | | a person | the curated rungs: thirteen abstracts, read on one day | **What breaks at scale.** Three things, in the order they bite: 1. **The politeness interval on public APIs.** The runtime is per-drug and dominated by waiting between requests, not by computation. Ten minutes for one card is fine; a thousand cards is not the same run repeated, it is a rate-limit and caching problem this pipeline does not solve. 2. **The curated rungs are the human bottleneck.** Rungs 2 and 3 exist only because a person read a paper — here, thirteen abstracts, one reader, one day (§10, item 5). The automated rungs scale freely; the rungs that carry the actual mechanism argument do not. 3. **One drug database was never queried.** DrugBank needs a licence for programmatic access, so it is absent from every count in this report (§10, item 6). At scale that is a licensing decision, not an engineering one. **A transfer onto a genuinely different case exists — and it is not this draft's.** The pipeline was run on a card for a different MVA gene, with its own disease identifiers, its own clinical terms, its own tumour context and no curated evidence. That run's tables are stamped 2026-09-19, **after this draft was written on 2026-09-18**; its claim is registered as H066 and its results belong to iteration 2: [`../iteration-2/report.md`](../iteration-2/report.md). **No number from that run appears in this report**, because this report is not written from it. --- ## 10. What this report cannot tell you > **Rubric:** Scientific Rigor — a report a panel can check is one that names its own > limits before the panel has to find them. 1. **Whether any of these drugs helps this child.** Rung 3 is one mouse paper; rung 2 is a dish. The challenge's words hold: hypotheses for follow-up. 2. **How aneuploid this child is.** The delivered data was tested with a statistic that has no power for mosaic gains; the powered analysis is planned (iteration 2, step 8) and has not run. Direction D2 inherits this gap entirely. 3. **Whether the weakened BubR1 copy is unstable or inactive.** It sits outside every catalogued domain; the structural model is confident about the region but says nothing about function. D3 is therefore argued as *more BubR1*, not *repair this BubR1*. 4. **Anything about a drug the public sources never listed** beyond what a person put in the curated table. Four of the eleven argued drugs (chloroquine, hydroxychloroquine, niacin, nicotinamide) are there only because a person read the paper; their rows say `curated_only`. 5. **The curated rungs are one person's reading of thirteen abstracts on one day.** Every row carries its PubMed id so the reading can be checked. 6. **DrugBank was not queried** (it needs a licence for programmatic access); Open Targets, ChEMBL, DGIdb, openFDA, Reactome, ClinicalTrials.gov and PubMed were. --- ## 11. Reproducibility > **Rubric:** Scalability and Scientific Rigor — the five commands that rebuild every > number in this report, and the cost of running them. Every step is one command, case-agnostic (swap the card, get another case), with a manifest: ```bash uv run mva-drugs snapshot # card → 5 tables, 7 public APIs, cached replies uv run python tools/track2_decoys.py ... # a decoy card and its snapshot (×2) uv run python tools/track2_enrich.py # literature, paediatric trials, labels, ladder, shortlist, do-not, decoy comparison uv run python tools/render_track2_figures.py # the figures in this report uv run python tools/record_track2_lineage.py # 63 lineage edges into the warehouse ledger ``` Runtime on a laptop: the snapshot ~10 minutes cold (mostly polite waiting between requests), the enrichment ~10 minutes cold, both seconds when cached. Code: the public repository named in the submission form; every table is under `ressources/track2/`, every entry under `docs/iteration2/step-7/`. **No patient data appears anywhere in Track 2** — gene symbols, drug names, trial ids and PubMed ids only; the mechanism card names allele *classes*, never positions. --- ## 12. Where every claim lives > **Rubric:** Scientific Rigor — each claim, its register id, its verdict and the entry > that tested it, so a reader can audit the reasoning rather than trust it. | claim | register id | verdict · confidence | entry | |---|---|---|---| | D1 yields no submittable drug and becomes the do-not table | H045 | supported · 0.80 | 113 | | D2 holds an approved compound with a molecule-level cell result | H046 | supported · 0.70 | 113 | | D3 has an approved route on the NAD⁺/SIRT2 axis with animal evidence, by proxy | H047 | supported · 0.60 | 113 | | D4 holds a non-chemotherapy approved drug at rung ≥ 2 with paediatric data | H048 | supported · 0.80 | 113 | | the automated stages are non-specific (a direction overlaps a decoy ≥ 0.10) | H049 | supported · 0.85 | 112 | | every argued drug has a paediatric pointer | H050 | supported · 0.70 | 113 | | no approved drug acts directly on BubR1 | H011 (iteration 1) | supported · 0.80 | 078 | Confidence is a transparent triage heuristic printed with its arithmetic, not a calibrated probability; the register is append-only and shows every revision, including one committed too early and corrected in the open (entry 113).

register.statement: The disease mechanism in this proband is hypomorphic loss of BUB1B function: one null allele (stop_gained, exon 17 of 23) plus one partly functional allele (kinase-domain missense), leaving reduced BubR1 and a leaky spindle assembly checkpoint; there is no gain-of-function or dominant-negative component.

No market-approved drug acts directly on BubR1; approved candidates for this case will come only from pathway neighbours (spindle assembly checkpoint members) and from aneuploidy-stress, proteostasis or tumour-context directions.

Direction D1 (checkpoint reinforcement) yields no submittable drug: no market-approved molecule strengthens the spindle assembly checkpoint or reduces chromosome missegregation in checkpoint-deficient cells, so every approved D1 candidate the sources return is a checkpoint inhibitor or a spindle poison and D1 becomes the do-not table.

Direction D2 (aneuploidy-selective stress) holds at least one market-approved compound with a cited result in aneuploid or checkpoint-deficient cell models, i.e. rung 2 or higher, and that evidence is for the approved molecule itself rather than only for an unapproved tool compound.

Direction D3 (BubR1 stabilisation for a hypomorph) has an approved-drug route: a market-approved agent acts on a BubR1-stabilising axis (SIRT2/NAD+ or acetylation) and the axis carries in-vivo evidence of raised BubR1 in a BubR1-insufficient model, i.e. rung 3, possibly through a same-axis proxy compound.

Direction D4 (the child's tumour context, rhabdomyosarcoma) holds at least one approved, non-cytotoxic agent with a cited mechanistic result in rhabdomyosarcoma models (rung 2 or higher) and with paediatric safety data.

The automated stages of the repurposing pipeline are not specific to the mechanism: with the clinical side held fixed and the gene swapped for a decoy (NTRK3, the seeded pick from the step-2 decoy set; XDH, an unrelated metabolic enzyme), at least one of the four directions' approved drug sets overlaps a decoy card's approved set at Jaccard 0.10 or more, so the curated rung, not the automated stage, is what separates candidates.

Every drug shortlisted at rung 2 or higher for the BUB1B card has paediatric data: an openFDA label with a pediatric_use section, or a ClinicalTrials.gov study that admits children, in any indication.

The Track 2 drug-repurposing pipeline is portable to a different case, not only a different gene: a TRIP13 / mosaic variegated aneuploidy syndrome 3 transfer card - its own disease and identifiers, its own HPO terms read out of phenotype.hpoa, its own nephroblastoma tumour context and standard of care, no alleles and no curated evidence - runs through mva-drugs snapshot and the step-7 enrichment with no code change and no hand-written query; the checkpoint-reinforcement direction D1 again yields no submittable drug and every D1 row stays at rung 1, and the spindle-poison anti-direction A2 again populates the do-not table.

From variant to mechanism to medicine in five documented stages, each a case-agnostic tool with a provenance manifest. (1) Hand-off: Track 1's confirmed compound-heterozygous BUB1B pair (a stop allele + a kinase-region missense, trans configuration confirmed by the challenge's answer key) was written into a structured 'mechanism card' (ressources/track2/mechanism.json): gene, protein, the two allele classes (never positions), loss-of-function reading, the spindle-assembly-checkpoint pathway, downstream consequences, the tumour context (rhabdomyosarcoma) from the clinical terms, and four repurposing directions with seed genes - D1 reinforce the checkpoint, D2 exploit aneuploidy stress, D3 stabilise the remaining BubR1 (hypomorph), D4 the child's tumour. Iteration 2 first rebuilt the genotype blind - a symptom-only target set with 396 matched decoy genes (step 1), alleles discovered from the raw reads without the vendor caller (step 2), alignment-free k-mer genotyping and copy number (step 3), a genome-wide likelihood-ratio ranking over 51,920 biallelic hypotheses (step 4), a public-knowledge route over 815 genes (step 5) and a rank fusion frozen by sha256 before it was compared (step 6): the same BUB1B pair came out first. Its measured facts (allele dosage, exon copy number, structural-variant absence, the missense's position in the protein, pathogenicity lanes, P(trans)) were appended as card revision v3, step 8's mosaic-aneuploidy bound (fold-over allele-balance statistic, 80 % power at 2-3 % of cells, no autosome above its limit in the sequenced sample) as revision v4, and step 8's second, independent instrument (k-mer dosage: one copy of X and one of Y recovered as a positive control, honest floor 1.6 % of cells) as revision v5. (2) Search: the card's seeds were expanded through Reactome pathways to 277 targets; Open Targets, ChEMBL and DGIdb returned 3,859 drug-target rows and 359 market-approved drugs; openFDA confirmed US labels; ClinicalTrials.gov and PubMed answered trial and literature questions, all queries derived from the card. (3) Grading: every approved drug on every direction was placed on a five-rung evidence ladder pre-registered before the search (5 approved for a related indication with paediatric use; 4 trial in a related indication; 3 animal model of the mechanism; 2 cell model; 1 mechanism only - named, never submitted). Automated tests (approval, label and its Pediatric Use section, tumour-context trials, studies admitting children, PubMed co-mention counts) and curated tests (one PubMed paper per row, read by a person, 13 rows) are printed side by side; inherited class-level evidence is marked 'proxy'. Every claim was registered with its prediction and its refutation condition before its test (one per direction, one for the control, one for paediatric data, one per card revision that the measured aneuploid fraction moves no rung, one for the transfer run); the card-revision tests were settled by byte-identical table digests, and the first of them caught a file-reading fault on the way. (4) Control: the same pipeline ran on two decoy cards - the child's clinical side kept, the gene swapped (NTRK3 by a seeded draw from Track 1's decoy set; XDH, an unrelated metabolic enzyme). A direction whose approved drugs overlap a decoy's at Jaccard >= 0.10 is reported as non-specific; D4 did (0.25) and is argued only from curated mechanism results. This decoy card is the pipeline's negative control: it answers 'what does the same machinery return for a gene that is not the cause?', and a direction that cannot beat it is demoted rather than argued. (5) Transfer: the same pipeline then ran unchanged on a transfer card that swaps the whole case, not only the gene - TRIP13 / mosaic variegated aneuploidy syndrome 3, its own OMIM/MONDO identifiers, its own 19 HPO terms read out of the public HPO annotation file (phenotype.hpoa release 2026-09-02) rather than typed, its own nephroblastoma tumour context and standard of care, no alleles and no curated literature. No module was edited and no query was hand-written; it produced 28 targets, 277 approved drugs, a 370-row evidence ladder, a 53-row shortlist and a do-not table, with a provenance manifest per file and one comparison row per case in ressources/track2/transfer_comparison.tsv. Only the automated rungs (1, 4, 5) compare, because a transfer card has no curated evidence.tsv by construction. The transfer's pre-registered claim (H066) was written as a conjunction of five limbs and came back REFUTED (0.10), recorded as refuted rather than reworded: four limbs held, including every limb that tests portability (the run completed with no module edit; all 30 checkpoint-direction rows stayed at rung 1; no mechanism-direction row reached the 53-row shortlist; only the tumour-context direction rose above rung 1), and the fifth failed - the spindle-poison anti-direction populated no row of the transfer do-not table. Diagnosed cause, recorded with it: that flag is a regular expression over each drug's action-type and mechanism-of-action text, which arrives through pathway expansion, and Reactome matched no pathway for the transfer gene, so all 1,329 candidate rows stayed at seed role with only 261 carrying any mechanism text. The operational consequence is stated in the report: a new case's pathway coverage must be checked before its do-not table is trusted. Output: 11 drugs with a cited mechanism result (statins; niacin/nicotinamide; chloroquine; bortezomib, metformin, valproic acid, vorinostat, hydroxychloroquine, atorvastatin), 50 drugs already in rhabdomyosarcoma trials listed as such, and a 23-drug do-not table (spindle poisons, checkpoint inhibitors, standard of care).

Both, kept apart and printed side by side. Automated: drug-target database queries (Open Targets, ChEMBL, DGIdb, Reactome, openFDA, ClinicalTrials.gov, PubMed E-utilities) driven by the mechanism card, plus per-drug PubMed co-mention counts and paediatric-trial lookups; these produce the candidate set and the automated rungs 4-5. Manual: the evidence rungs 2-3 come from 13 papers read by a person and entered in evidence.tsv with the PubMed id, the model (cell / in vivo) and a proxy flag when the paper tested a same-axis compound rather than the approved drug. LLM assistance was used to draft queries, code and prose; every PubMed id was resolved live against E-utilities before it was written down, and four ids first recalled from memory were wrong and replaced by title search before entering any file.

Thirteen curated rows, each one cited result: Tang & Amon 2011 (PMID 21315436) - chloroquine and the AMPK activator AICAR are aneuploidy-selective in trisomic and aneuploid cells (rung 2 for chloroquine; metformin and hydroxychloroquine inherit as proxies); Ippolito 2024 (39247952) and Chui 2019 (31530568) - aneuploid cells depend on protein degradation and are more sensitive to proteasome inhibition (bortezomib, class proxy); North 2014 (24825348) - the NAD+ precursor NMN raised BubR1 in vivo and SIRT2 extended the lifespan of BubR1-hypomorphic mice (rung 3; niacin and nicotinamide as proxies); Park 2017 (28985013) and Choi 2009 (19407811) - HDAC2/3 deacetylation drives BubR1 degradation, acetylation protects it (valproic acid, vorinostat as class proxies); Gizaw 2025 (41249736) - lovastatin itself reduced rhabdomyosarcoma cell proliferation and cholesterol synthesis is a non-redundant tumour vulnerability (rung 2; simvastatin and atorvastatin as proxies). The anti-directions rest on Suijkerbuijk 2010 (20516114, MVA cells have a weakened checkpoint), Sinha 2019 (30601084, mitotic slippage) and Cohen-Sharir 2021 (33505028, aneuploid cells are killed by checkpoint inhibition). The mechanism section rests on Hanks 2004 (15475955) and Suijkerbuijk 2010. Curation was one person's reading of the abstracts on 2026-09-18; every row carries its PubMed id so it can be checked.
Publicly available sources only. No proprietary data source was used.

Open Targets Platform (GraphQL API, drugAndClinicalCandidates per target and disease), ChEMBL (REST: target search, mechanism, molecule max_phase, first approval, ATC), DGIdb (GraphQL interactions), Reactome ContentService (pathways containing the protein, participants), openFDA drug labels (current US label; the pediatric_use section), ClinicalTrials.gov v2 (studies by condition and intervention; aggFilters=ages:child for studies admitting children), PubMed E-utilities (esearch counts and ids, esummary), plus ClinVar (the stop allele's classification) and gnomAD (population absence of the missense) from Track 1. DrugBank was named by the form but not queried: its programmatic access needs a licence. Every reply is cached and its digest rolled into the table's manifest; retrieval dates are 2026-09-05 (first snapshot) and 2026-09-18 (refresh and enrichment).
None.

Loss of function, hypomorphic, of a confirmed compound heterozygote. One allele is a stop change in exon 17 of 23 (ClinVar pathogenic / likely pathogenic for MVA syndrome 1): no functional BubR1 from that copy. The other is a missense change in the last exon: absent from gnomAD, AlphaMissense likely-pathogenic (log-likelihood-ratio lane 4.33), CADD 24.5, sitting outside every InterPro domain-typed entry in a region AlphaFold models at pLDDT 91 - a weakened copy, not a dead one, consistent with every published MVA1 genotype (complete loss is embryonic-lethal). No gain-of-function or dominant-negative activity is reported for BUB1B. Trans configuration: confirmed by the oracle's full match at rank 1 (population phasing was undetermined; read-backed phase blocks did not reach the gene). Dosage: both alleles at one-copy multiplicity in the raw reads by an alignment-free k-mer method; every exon at two copies; no structural variant in the gene. Pathway: the spindle assembly checkpoint - BubR1 is a core component of the mitotic checkpoint complex that inhibits APC/C-CDC20 and recruits PP2A-B56 to kinetochores; less BubR1 gives a leaky checkpoint (Suijkerbuijk 2010 measured strongly reduced BubR1 and a weakened checkpoint in MVA cells). Downstream: premature anaphase and chromosome missegregation; mosaic variegated aneuploidy; proteotoxic and metabolic stress in aneuploid cells; cancer predisposition (rhabdomyosarcoma - the child's presenting tumour - Wilms tumour, leukaemia); growth restriction and nephrocalcinosis, which are the delivered clinical terms. Aneuploid fraction: measured in iteration 2's step 8 by two instruments that share nothing past the raw reads. Instrument 1, allele balance: a fold-over B-allele-deviation statistic with 80 % power at 2 % (chr1-6) and 3 % (chr7-22) of cells finds no autosome above its own detection limit in the sequenced sample (the statistic used earlier, the mean B-allele fraction per megabase, had no power at any fraction tested); it cannot read X or Y in a male. Instrument 2, k-mer dosage (reference-unique 31-mers over 32 of 272 flowcell shards): recovers one copy of X at 0.4873 and one of Y at 0.5083 against 0.5 expected - the positive control allele balance cannot supply - and puts no autosome beyond its composition-corrected null (chromosome-GC regressor, Pearson 0.904, 81.7 % of the between-chromosome spread explained, residual spread 0.802 %); the one chromosome that looked suspicious under a bootstrap interval (chr21, 2.33 sigma, Bonferroni p 0.43) dissolved under tail trimming, a probe half-split and a depth check that read the excess as mismapping pileups. Honest floor: 1.6 % of cells, twice the residual spread. Still outside both routes: events smaller than a chromosome arm, and copy-neutral loss of heterozygosity, which moves no sequence for the dosage route to see; and the sequenced tissue is not named by the delivery, so this is a statement about the sample and not the diagnosis. Consequence for the drug argument: direction D2 (aneuploidy-selective stress) is argued from published aneuploid-cell biology only and ranked below D3 and D4. Open: whether the missense copy is unstable or catalytically inactive - so D3 is argued as raising BubR1 abundance, not as refolding it.

Roughly five working days across two people-equivalents for Track 2 itself (the card and data layer on 2026-09-05/06; the claims, ladder, decoy control, curation, figures, dashboard and report on 2026-09-18; the card revision from step 8 and this report on 2026-09-19), on top of the fortnight of iteration-2 genotype work (steps 1-6 and 8) the mechanism facts come from. Compute for Track 2: two laptop runs of about ten minutes against public APIs; no cloud, no paid data source, so the marginal money cost of a run is zero. Measured cost of adding a case the pipeline had never seen (the TRIP13 transfer run, cold cache): 2,077 live requests and 1,693.7 s of wall clock end to end on the same laptop, of which about 706 s is the enforced 0.34 s politeness interval between live calls; re-deriving the same tables from the warm cache afterwards took 9.0 s. The real case's own 85 live requests are not comparable, because they were measured against a cache 1,965 replies deep.

Question. Given a confirmed compound-heterozygous loss of BUB1B (a stop allele and a hypomorphic kinase-region missense) in a child with mosaic variegated aneuploidy and rhabdomyosarcoma, which market-approved drugs act on the mechanism, and how strong is the evidence for each? Method. We first rebuilt the genotype blind from the raw reads and the eight clinical terms - symptom-only target set with matched decoys, alleles from the reads without the vendor caller, alignment-free genotyping, a genome-wide likelihood ranking, a knowledge route, and a rank fusion frozen by digest before comparison - and found the same pair first. A structured mechanism card carries the confirmed pair and nine measured facts. The ninth, step 8's mosaic-aneuploidy bound, is now measured by two instruments sharing nothing past the raw reads: allele balance (80 % power at 2-3 % of cells; no autosome above its limit) and k-mer dosage, recovering one copy each of X and Y as a positive control and setting a 1.6 % floor. The card drives every query: Reactome expands its seeds to 277 targets; Open Targets, ChEMBL and DGIdb return 359 approved drugs; openFDA, ClinicalTrials.gov and PubMed answer label, trial and literature questions per drug. Every drug on every direction sits on a five-rung ladder pre-registered before the search, automated tests beside 13 person-curated PubMed rows, inherited class evidence flagged as proxy. Claims were registered with predictions and refutation conditions before their tests. Controls: two decoy cards (same child, gene swapped) and a transfer card swapping the whole case (TRIP13 / MVA syndrome 3, nephroblastoma, its own phenotype terms read from public annotation), both run unchanged. Results. D1 (reinforce the checkpoint) has no approved drug and became the do-not table. D3 (raise BubR1): NAD+ repletion raised BubR1 in BubR1-hypomorphic mice, inherited by niacin and nicotinamide (rung 3); HDAC inhibitors act on BubR1's acetylation switch at class level. D4 (the tumour): lovastatin itself slowed rhabdomyosarcoma cells, and a completed paediatric phase-1 trial gave simvastatin in relapsed solid tumours. D2 (aneuploidy stress): chloroquine has a molecule-level cell result, but the direction is literature-only and ranked last: the sequenced sample shows no aneuploid population for such a drug to act on. Eleven drugs carry a cited mechanism result; fifty more reach the top rung only as tumour-trial context, listed not claimed; 23 sit in the do-not table, among them 13 spindle poisons relying on the very checkpoint that is broken. The decoy control showed D4's automated stage non-specific (Jaccard 0.25) and exposed a grading flaw, corrected before any verdict; two pre-registered digest tests showed neither card revision moved a rung; the transfer case produced a complete output with no code change, D1 again empty. Limitations. Curated rungs are one reader's; rung 3 is one mouse paper; the aneuploidy bound covers whole chromosomes and arms in a sample whose tissue is unnamed; the transfer case has no curated evidence, so only automated rungs compare; DrugBank was not queried. Hypotheses for follow-up, not evidence that any medicine works.

# Track 2 report — from a confirmed genotype to graded, approved medicines, with its own negative control **Standing:** draft, written 2026-09-19, revised 2026-09-20 from executed runs. Iteration 2 of Track 2 supersedes [iteration 1](../iteration-1/report.md) (never uploaded): the mechanism card is at **version 5** with all nine measured facts filled — the last one, the aneuploid fraction in the sequenced sample, by iteration 2's step 8, now on **two instruments that share nothing past the raw reads** — and the report tells the whole path, steps 1 to 8, plus a **transfer run** of the same pipeline on a second, different case. Every number is read from a table with a provenance manifest; every claim was registered before its test; every cited paper was resolved against PubMed. **Not uploaded.** Track 2 accepts one submission (due about 2026-10-20). Written for a panel that includes clinicians and patient advocates as well as scientists. Each technical term appears once with its meaning in brackets; the full dictionary is served at `/learn` on the dashboard, and the same tables render on its `/track2` page. > The challenge's own words, kept in view throughout: *submissions are hypotheses for > follow-up, not evidence that a medicine works.* Nothing below is a recommendation to treat. --- ## 1. How this report answers the panel's four questions > **Rubric:** all four — this is the map; every row names the section that carries the work and > the softest spot we know in it. | criterion | weight | where | the evidence, in one line | the weakest point we know | |---|---|---|---|---| | **Scientific rigor** — is the mechanism sound, and is the drug argument built on it? | 35 % | §2–§7 | a genotype confirmed by the challenge's own answer key and then **rediscovered blind**; nine measured facts on a versioned mechanism card, the last on two independent instruments; every approved drug graded on a ladder written **before** the search, with a decoy gene through the same pipeline as a negative control | the two rungs that carry the argument (a result in an animal, a result in a dish) are **13 abstracts read by one person on one day**; the deepest mechanistic lead is a single mouse paper, inherited by two vitamin forms; **no** drug has a molecule-level animal result on the checkpoint itself | | **Potential impact** — what could this change if it validated? | 25 % | §8 | a do-not table that turns the mechanism into one concrete question for the treating team; a mechanism-level (not gene-level) conclusion that reaches the other MVA genes; a **sequencing-only** bound on mosaic aneuploidy with a stated detection limit, where the classical test needs cells that grow | nothing here has been tested in this child or in any patient; the do-not table weighs a mechanism hypothesis against regimens that have survival data behind them; the aneuploidy bound is a statement about a sample whose **tissue the delivery never named** | | **Innovation** — is the angle genuinely new? | 25 % | §9 | one structured card drives every query; a pre-registered evidence ladder; a decoy gene *and* a whole transfer case as controls; a do-not table as a first-class output; an append-only claim register where each claim carries its refutation condition and corrections stay visible | every part is standard on its own — public APIs, a rubric, a register. What we claim is the **assembly**, and only "to our knowledge": we did not run a literature survey. Knowledge-graph repurposing rankers exist (PrimeKG, TxGNN — §9) and we did not run them | | **Scalability** — does this reach other people and other diseases? | 15 % | §10 | the pipeline was **executed unchanged** on a transfer case with a different MVA gene, a different disease, a different tumour and its own phenotype terms read out of a public annotation file: a second complete output, at **0 lines of code changed** and 0 hand-typed queries | our own pre-registered claim about the transfer came back **refuted** (H066 · 0.10): four limbs held, including every limb that tests portability, but the spindle-poison caution **did not fire** on the transfer case, because the public pathway database had no annotation for that gene. So the **automated safety half degrades on a new gene with thin pathway coverage** — a new case needs that coverage checked before its do-not table is trusted (§10.5). Also: one transfer case, sharing the same pathway; only the **automated** rungs compare, because a transfer card has no curated literature, and the curated rungs that carry the drug argument stay a human bottleneck | --- ## 2. The answer in one page > **Rubric:** scientific rigor (35 %) — the claim, the confirmed genotype behind it, and what is not known, on one page. **The child.** A boy with mosaic variegated aneuploidy (MVA: some of his cells carry a wrong number of chromosomes, and different cells are wrong in different ways), short stature, failure to thrive, calcium deposits in the kidneys, and a rhabdomyosarcoma (a childhood cancer of muscle tissue). Eight clinical terms were delivered with the case; no karyotype was. **The cause, found twice.** Track 1 found two different broken copies of one gene, `BUB1B` — one from each parent (a *compound heterozygote*) — and the challenge's answer key confirmed the pair with a full match at rank 1. Iteration 2 then rebuilt the answer **blind**, from the raw reads and the eight clinical terms, by routes sharing no code with the first: the same pair came out first. The gene makes BubR1, the **brake** on cell division that holds a dividing cell until every chromosome is attached. One copy makes nothing (a *stop* change); the other makes a weakened protein (a *missense* change in the protein's last stretch). Less brake, not no brake — the only pattern compatible with life, and the pattern every published case shows. **Nine measured facts** sit on the mechanism card (now at version 5) so that no drug argument rests on the allele labels alone. The one that matters most for this report: **no chromosome in the sequenced sample carries a mosaic population above 2–3 % of cells** (step 8, at 80 % power), where the statistic used earlier would have found nothing at any fraction. That bound is now carried by **two instruments that share nothing past the raw reads** — allele balance, and a k-mer dosage route that reads the sex chromosomes the first is blind to, recovering one copy of X (0.4873) and one of Y (0.5083) against 0.5 expected as its positive control, and setting an honest floor of **1.6 % of cells** on what it could have detected. It is a statement about the sequenced sample — its tissue is not named by the delivery, and a karyotype's fraction is measured in cultured cells — not about the diagnosis. **Four ways a drug could act, graded on a five-rung ladder written before the search**, then run again with the gene swapped for two decoys as a control: | Direction | The idea | What we found | Standing after step 8 | |---|---|---|---| | **D1** reinforce the brake | strengthen the remaining checkpoint | **no approved drug does this**; every checkpoint drug on the market or in trials *weakens* it | the do-not table | | **D3** raise the amount of working BubR1 | the weakened copy still works — make more of it last longer | **niacin / nicotinamide** (vitamin B3 forms): boosting the NAD⁺ pathway raised BubR1 in mice bred with too little of it (rung 3, animal model, by proxy); valproic acid and vorinostat act on BubR1's acetylation switch (rung 2, class level) | **the deepest mechanistic lead** — acts on the constitutional genotype whatever the burden; thinnest automated support | | **D4** the child's actual tumour | approved, non-chemotherapy drugs with a mechanism in rhabdomyosarcoma | **statins**: rhabdomyosarcoma cells depend on making their own cholesterol; lovastatin itself slowed them (rung 2, molecule level); simvastatin has been in a completed paediatric sarcoma trial (NCT02390843) | **the best-supported lead** — a molecule-level result and a paediatric trial agree | | **D2** exploit the stress of aneuploid cells | aneuploid cells are already stressed; some approved drugs tip them over | **chloroquine** preferentially killed aneuploid cells in the reference screen (rung 2, molecule level); metformin, hydroxychloroquine, bortezomib inherit class results | **literature only** — the sequenced sample shows no aneuploid population ≥ 2–3 % for such a drug to act on; a tumour-context angle, not a treatment of the child's state | **What not to do — the half a clinician may care about most.** Thirteen approved drugs are *spindle poisons*: they jam cell division and rely on the checkpoint to hold the cell. In a child whose checkpoint is the broken part, that reliance is a hypothesis worth weighing. Vincristine and vinorelbine are standard rhabdomyosarcoma chemotherapy. **This report flags the question for the treating team; it does not advise withholding standard care.** No approved drug weakens the checkpoint further — that class exists only in trials, and it is the one to avoid. **What we do not know.** Whether any drug on this page helps (rung 3 is one mouse paper). Whether the weakened BubR1 copy is unstable or simply inactive. What tissue was sequenced. Anything about events smaller than a chromosome arm, or about a copy-neutral swap that moves no sequence for the dosage route to see. --- ## 3. We have no clinical outcome data, no dose-response in this genotype, and no patient-level evidence of any kind | | **What would settle it** | a checkpoint-function readout (how long cells carrying these allele classes hold mitosis under a spindle challenge, and whether they die or slip) — a bench question, not a chart question | **The one experiment we would run next.** The deepest mechanistic lead, D3 (raise the amount of working BubR1), rests on rung 3 **by proxy**: a NAD⁺ precursor, NMN, raised BubR1 in mice bred to be BubR1-deficient (North 2014, PMID 24825348). That is an animal result, on a related compound, in a different genotype. One experiment would lift it to molecule level in this genotype: - **Material** — cells carrying this child's allele classes: patient-derived fibroblasts, or an engineered line with one stop allele and one last-exon missense. - **Treatment** — nicotinamide and niacin (the two approved vitamin-B3 forms this report argues), across a dose range, against vehicle. - **Read-outs** — (1) BubR1 protein abundance; (2) checkpoint function: how long a cell holds mitosis under a spindle challenge; (3) chromosome missegregation rate. - **Prediction, written first** — BubR1 abundance rises with dose, and arrest duration lengthens with it. - **What would refute it** — no rise in BubR1 at any tolerated dose. That result would say the rung-3 animal evidence does not transfer to this genotype, and D3 should be dropped rather than softened. - **Status — proposal. Not run. No result is claimed for it.** It needs a wet lab and cells this project never had; it is written here in the same pre-registered shape as every claim in §13 so that it can be filed before it is run rather than after. ### 8.2 For others living with MVA: the conclusions are about the mechanism, not the gene Three genes are established causes of MVA: `BUB1B` (MVA1) and `TRIP13` (MVA3), both parts of the same mitotic-checkpoint machinery, and `CEP57` (MVA2), a centrosome part ([dictionary](../../../docs/dictionary.md)). Two results in this report are therefore properties of **a weakened mitotic checkpoint**, not of this child's gene: | result | why it is a mechanism property | what it means for another family | |---|---|---| | **no approved drug reinforces the checkpoint** (D1 is empty; every checkpoint drug on the market or in trials *weakens* it) | the direction is defined by the pathway, and the pathway is what MVA1 and MVA3 share | the same gap exists for them. It is also a concrete ask for drug developers: the direction this disease needs has **zero** approved entries | | **the spindle-poison caution** | it rests on "the checkpoint holds the cell", which is the mechanism, not the gene | it applies to any constitutionally checkpoint-deficient child facing this drug class, with the same "weigh it, never withhold" framing | This is not a claim we are asking the panel to take on trust — it was **executed**. The pipeline was re-run on a transfer card for `TRIP13` / MVA3 (a different gene, a different disease, a different tumour), and direction D1 returned **30 drugs, every one of them at rung 1** — mechanism only, named and never submitted. The same empty answer, reached again, with no code changed (§10). The honest other half: on that case the spindle-poison caution produced **no** rows at all, for a reason §10 states. ### 8.3 For diagnosis: a sequencing-only bound on mosaic aneuploidy, with its limit stated The classical test for MVA is a **karyotype** (counting chromosomes down a microscope in cells first grown in culture). It needs cells that will grow, and it reports a fraction of the cells that grew. Step 8 asks the same question of DNA sequence alone, twice over, and — this is the part that matters — reports **what it could have detected**: | | sequencing-only bound (step 8, two instruments) | |---|---| | **what it can do** | put a number on how much mosaic whole-chromosome or whole-arm aneuploidy could be hiding in the sequenced sample — no autosome above **2 % of cells** (chr1–6) or **3 %** (chr7–22) at 80 % power by allele balance, and an honest floor of **1.6 % of cells** by k-mer dosage; read **X and Y**, which allele balance cannot in a male, recovering one copy of each (0.4873, 0.5083 against 0.5) as a positive control on a known answer; and do all of it from data already sequenced, with no extra sample and no culture | | **what it cannot replace** | a karyotype, for diagnosis. It is blind to events smaller than a chromosome arm, and the dosage route is blind by construction to a copy-neutral swap (the right number of chromosomes from the wrong parent), which moves no sequence for it to see | | **what it cannot say** | anything about a tissue that was not sequenced. **The delivery never named the tissue of this sample.** MVA is *variegated* — different cells carry different errors — so a bound in one tissue is not a bound in another | | **what it is, precisely** | a **bound**, not a measurement: "nothing above the floor", never "zero" | The transferable point is smaller than a new diagnostic and more useful than it sounds: **a negative result is only a result when it carries its detection limit.** This project's own step 0 produced a flat karyogram with no detection limit; step 8 corrected it on exactly that point (§4). Any pipeline that reports "no aneuploidy found" without a floor is reporting nothing. --- ## 9. What is new here, against standard practice > **Rubric:** innovation (25 %) — what this pipeline does that a repurposing write-up usually > does not, stated as a comparison and hedged to "to our knowledge". | what a repurposing report usually does | what this one does | |---|---| | queries typed by hand into each database, per drug or per gene, and re-typed for the next case | **one structured mechanism card** (`ressources/track2/mechanism.json`: gene, allele classes, pathway, measured facts, directions, seed genes, the ladder) drives **every** query. No query string is typed by hand. The card is versioned and append-only — v3 → v4 → v5, each revision a `history` entry with the entries behind it | | produces a ranked list of candidate drugs | produces an **evidence ladder written before the search**, with the **automated** test (approval, label section, registered trials) and the **person-read** test (one PubMed id per row) printed side by side and never merged into one score. Rung 1 is *named, never submitted* | | has no negative control — nothing says what the same pipeline returns for the wrong gene | runs a **decoy gene** through the same pipeline and measures the overlap against a threshold fixed beforehand (Jaccard 0.10). D4 failed it at 0.25, so D4 is argued only from curated mechanism results — a direction demoted by its own control (§6.3) | | covers one case, and generality is asserted | covers a **transfer case**: a card that swaps the gene, the disease, the tumour and the clinical terms, executed unchanged, with both cases' counts in one committed table (§10) | | lists candidates | ships a **do-not table as a first-class output**: caution, do-not, and standard-of-care verdicts, with the reason and the citation per row (§7.3) | | asserts confidence after the fact | files each claim in an **append-only register before its test**, with its prediction *and* its refutation condition; confidence is a printed heuristic shown with its arithmetic, never a probability; corrections stay visible — two verdicts committed too early are in the record beside their corrections (§13) | **Prior art, named accurately.** Knowledge-graph repurposing rankers exist and are strong at the step this pipeline deliberately does not take. **PrimeKG** (a disease-centric biomedical knowledge graph, PMID 36732524) and **TxGNN** (a graph neural network that scores drugs against a disease node, including diseases with no approved drug, PMID 39322717) both take a **disease node** as input and return a ranked drug list. This repository keeps notes on both (`docs/iteration4/cards/primekg.json`, `docs/iteration4/cards/txgnn.json`, both MIT-licensed) and **neither was run for this report.** The difference is the input and the shape of the output: they rank from a disease; this pipeline argues from **one patient's measured mechanism**, and returns a graded argument with a negative control and a do-not list rather than a rank. **How strongly we put it:** each ingredient above is standard on its own — public APIs, a grading rubric, a pre-registration habit, a decoy control. What we claim is the **assembly**, and only *to our knowledge*: we have not seen a drug-repurposing write-up that ships a decoy control, a whole transfer case and an append-only claim register together. That is our reading of what we have read, not a literature survey, and we would rather be corrected than overstate it. --- ## 10. Scalability: the same pipeline, a second case > **Rubric:** scalability (15 %) — executed evidence that this reaches another person, another > disease and another dataset, together with the pre-registered claim it **refuted**. ### 10.1 What was swapped The decoy control (§6.3) swaps the *gene* and keeps the child: it measures **specificity**. The transfer run swaps the **whole case** and measures **portability** — does the same code, with no edit and no hand-written query, produce the same tables for a case it was never written for? | | the real case | the transfer case | |---|---|---| | gene | `BUB1B` | `TRIP13` | | disease | MVA1 (OMIM 257300, MONDO:0009759) | MVA3 (OMIM 617598, MONDO:0054736) | | clinical terms | the 8 HPO terms delivered with the case | **19 terms read out of** the public HPO annotation file (`phenotype.hpoa`, release 2026-09-02) for OMIM:617598 — *read, never typed*; `NOT`-qualified rows skipped | | tumour context | rhabdomyosarcoma | nephroblastoma (Wilms tumour) | | standard of care | 12 drugs | 5 drugs, taken only from resolved abstracts | | alleles | 2 confirmed allele classes | **none** — the transfer card asserts no variant in any person | | curated literature | 13 person-read rows | **none** — a transfer card has no `evidence.tsv` by construction | | copied from the template card | — | exactly **3 case-agnostic blocks**: the anti-directions, the evidence ladder, the eligibility constraints. Everything case-shaped is built from the spec | Nothing was inherited from the child: `mva.drugs.transfer` reads the OMIM id, never the delivery. ### 10.2 The two cases side by side ![The same pipeline's output on both cases, count by count](../../../figures/track2/transfer-scalability.png) > **Legend** — one group per count, one bar per case, **linear** axis and no normalisation: > **blue = the real case** (`BUB1B` / MVA1), **purple = the transfer case** (`TRIP13` / MVA3). > The point is that both cases produced a table of the same *shape*, so a ratio would hide which > is bigger. **`curated evidence rows` is plotted precisely because it is zero** for the transfer > case — that zero is the boundary of what this comparison may claim, not a gap in the data. > Source: `ressources/track2/transfer_comparison.tsv`, one row per case, with its manifest. | | real case (`BUB1B` / MVA1) | transfer case (`TRIP13` / MVA3) | |---|---|---| | target genes | 277 | 28 | | drug–target candidate rows | 3,859 | 1,329 | | distinct approved drugs | 359 | 277 | | drugs at best rung 5 / 3 / 2 / 1 | 62 / 2 / 5 / 260 | 55 / 0 / 0 / 210 | | shortlist rows | 61 | 53 (**every one** `context trial only`, on the tumour direction) | | do-not rows | 23 | 3 (all *standard of care*) | | curated evidence rows | 13 | **0** | | modules edited to run it | — | **0** | Two results carry over and one does not: - **D1 is empty again.** All 30 checkpoint-reinforcement rows sit at rung 1 — no submittable drug — and none reaches the shortlist. "No approved drug reinforces the checkpoint" is a property of the mechanism, reproduced on a second gene (§8.2). - **No trial leaked onto a mechanism direction.** Only the tumour direction D4 reaches rung 2 or higher (55 rows at rung 5); D1 (30), D2 (82) and D3 (39) stay entirely at rung 1 — the narrowing recorded in entry 113 holds on a card it was not written for. - **The spindle-poison caution did not fire.** The transfer's do-not table holds 3 rows, all standard of care, and **no** row anywhere carries the `A2` flag (real case: 13). §10.5 says why. ### 10.3 What it cost | | measured | |---|---| | wall clock, a case the pipeline had never seen (cold cache) | **1,693.7 s** end to end, snapshot + enrichment, on the same laptop | | live requests, cold | **2,077**; cached replies 0 | | re-deriving the same tables afterwards (warm cache) | **9.0 s** | | money | **€0** — seven public APIs, no cloud, no licensed data source | | human time to author the case | one spec file (§10.4). The clinical terms are read from a public file, not written | **The asymmetry, stated.** The real case's row reads **85 live requests against 1,965 cached** — a *warm* re-run over a cache filled by earlier runs. The transfer's is the *cold* pass that filled its own. **The comparable figure is the transfer's cold pass**, and it is the one quoted whenever this report says what a new case costs. ### 10.4 What authoring a new case actually takes One committed spec file. Abbreviated from `ressources/track2/transfer/TRIP13/transfer_spec.json` — the fields a person writes: ```jsonc { "gene": { "symbol": "TRIP13", "uniprot": "Q15645", "hgnc_id": "HGNC:12307", "_verified": "UniProt REST + HGNC REST, 2026-09-20" }, "case": { "disease": "Mosaic variegated aneuploidy syndrome 3 (MVA3)", "omim_phenotype": "617598", "mondo": "MONDO:0054736", "tumour_context": "nephroblastoma (Wilms tumour; HP:0002667)", "context_standard_of_care": { "drugs": ["VINCRISTINE", "…"], "source": "PMID 41223336, 42686227" } }, "repurposing_directions": [ { "id": "D3", "name": "TRIP13 / p31comet proteostasis axis", "rationale": "…a loss-of-function AAA+ ATPase is a protein-remodelling problem…", "seed_targets": ["TRIP13", "MAD2L1BP", "VCP", "PSMB5", "HSP90AA1", "HSPA8"], "context": false }, { "id": "D4", "name": "cancer surveillance in the nephroblastoma context", "seed_targets": ["WT1", "IGF2", "IGF1R", "CTNNB1", "TP53", "MTOR", "VEGFA"], "context": true } ], "hpo_source": { "_note": "filled in from phenotype.hpoa at build time — read, never typed" } } ``` What that buys: the disease identifiers drive every disease query; `context: true` marks the one direction the trial-based rungs may grade; `seed_targets` are expanded through Reactome; the phenotype terms are read from a public file. What it does **not** buy: the curated rungs (§10.5). Every identifier in the committed spec was resolved live against UniProt, HGNC, EBI OLS4 and PubMed before the file was committed; anything that would not resolve is recorded as `null` with a note rather than guessed. ### 10.5 What breaks at scale — including a claim of ours that broke **Our own pre-registered claim came back refuted, and is reported as refuted.** H066 said the pipeline is portable *and* the spindle-poison anti-direction would again populate the do-not table. Four of its five limbs held — including every limb that tests portability — and the fourth failed against a refutation condition written before the run. Filed as a conjunction, a false limb refutes it as written: **H066 · refuted · 0.10** (entry [138](../../../docs/iteration2/step-7/methodology/138-a-second-case-through-the-same-pipeline.md)). The grading heuristic suggested 0.98 — it sums evidence rows and cannot see that a claim is an AND — and that suggestion was rejected on the record. | what breaks | the measured detail | what it means | |---|---|---| | **an anti-direction is only as good as the text it matches** | the `A2` flag is a regular expression over each drug's action-type and mechanism-of-action text. Reactome matched **0** pathways for `TRIP13`, so `pathways.tsv` is header-only and all 1,329 candidate rows stay at `target_role = seed`, with only 261 carrying any mechanism text. The real case has **2,276** rows from pathway expansion and 11 of its 13 `A2` drugs arrive on one. Two spindle poisons *are* in the transfer candidate set but reach it from DGIdb with empty mechanism text | the do-not table is a **derived** artefact of how much mechanism text the candidate set happens to carry, not a property of the card. A gene the pathway database cannot expand gets a nearly empty do-not table while the same drugs sit in its candidate set unflagged. **Not fixed here**: widening the flag would change the ladder rule and must be filed as its own pre-registered test, not folded into a refuted claim | | **the politeness interval on public APIs** | a minimum **0.34 s** between live calls (NCBI's 3 requests/second without an API key), single-threaded. 2,077 live requests ≈ **706 s** of enforced waiting — about 40 % of the cold pass | throughput per case is bounded by courtesy, not by compute. Going faster needs API keys and per-source agreements, not a bigger machine | | **the curated rungs are the human bottleneck** | rungs 2 and 3 exist only where a person read a paper: 13 rows for the real case, **0** for the transfer case. Its 53 shortlist rows are therefore *all* `context trial only` — **not one argued drug** | the automated half scales to a new case in 28 minutes; the half that carries the argument does not scale at all yet. A bigger shortlist is not a better one | | **one drug database left unqueried** | **DrugBank** needs a licence for programmatic access; Open Targets, ChEMBL, DGIdb, openFDA, Reactome, ClinicalTrials.gov and PubMed were queried | coverage is what the open sources cover, on both cases equally | | **what the transfer case did not get** | no alleles, no curated literature, no measured facts of its own | **only the automated stages (rungs 1, 4, 5) compare.** `curated_rows` is printed beside every count so the boundary is visible rather than implied | | **one case, one pathway** | `TRIP13` shares the spindle assembly checkpoint with `BUB1B` — chosen so that a transfer that works is a statement about the pipeline, not about how unalike the cases are | portability to a disease *outside* this pathway is untested. It would be a new claim, filed before it is run | **The operational rule this buys.** A new case's do-not table is only as complete as its pathway coverage. Before the automated safety half of this pipeline is trusted on a new gene, check that the pathway expansion returned something: an empty `pathways.tsv` means the anti-direction flags cannot fire, whatever the card says. That check is a measured boundary of the transfer, found because a refutation condition was written before the run. **What this section does not claim.** Not that the transfer case's output is clinically useful — it is a demonstration that the code is case-agnostic, asserts no allele in any person, and is not a drug suggestion for anyone with MVA3. And portability itself is the *finding* of entry 138, resting on the four limbs that held; it is not asserted by H066's verdict, which is a verdict on the conjunction. --- ## 11. What this report cannot tell you > **Rubric:** scientific rigor (35 %) — the limits of everything above, stated as limits. 1. **Whether any of these drugs helps this child.** Rung 3 is one mouse paper; rung 2 is a dish. Hypotheses for follow-up. 2. **What tissue was sequenced, and therefore what F8 means for the diagnosis.** The delivery does not name it; a karyotype's fraction is measured in cultured cells. F8 says the sequenced sample carries no mosaic population above 2–3 % on any autosome (allele balance) and none above a 1.6 % floor (k-mer dosage, which also reads X and Y and recovers one copy of each). What neither route can see: events **smaller than a chromosome arm**, and a copy-neutral swap that moves no sequence for the dosage route to read. 3. **Whether the weakened BubR1 copy is unstable or inactive.** Outside every catalogued domain; the structure model is confident about the region but silent on function. 4. **Anything about a drug the public sources never listed** beyond what a person put in the curated table — four of the eleven (chloroquine, hydroxychloroquine, niacin, nicotinamide) are there only because a person read the paper; their rows say `curated_only`. 5. **The curated rungs are one reader's**, thirteen abstracts on one day; every row carries its PubMed id so it can be checked. 6. **DrugBank was not queried** (licence); Open Targets, ChEMBL, DGIdb, openFDA, Reactome, ClinicalTrials.gov and PubMed were. --- ## 12. Reproducibility and cost > **Rubric:** scalability (15 %) and scientific rigor (35 %) — what it costs to re-run, and whether a reader can. Every step is one command, case-agnostic, with a manifest and a lineage row; no patient data appears in any Track 2 artefact (gene symbols, allele *classes*, drug names, trial ids, PubMed ids only): ```bash uv run mva-drugs snapshot # card → 5 tables, 7 public APIs, cached replies uv run python tools/track2_decoys.py ... # a decoy card and its snapshot (×2) uv run python tools/track2_enrich.py # literature, paediatric trials, labels, ladder, shortlist, do-not, decoy comparison uv run python tools/render_track2_figures.py # the figures in this report uv run python tools/record_track2_lineage.py # the lineage edges into the warehouse ledger uv run python tools/track2_transfer.py # the whole pipeline again, on a second case (§10) ``` Two laptop runs of about ten minutes each against public APIs, seconds when cached; a case the pipeline has never seen costs **1,693.7 s and 2,077 live requests** end to end, measured (§10). The genotype steps 1–6 and 8 ran on a laptop and one Linux server over a fortnight (their methodology entries state each cost). Code and tables: the public repository named in the form; the dashboard's `/track2` page renders the same tables with the grading visible. ## 13. Where every claim lives > **Rubric:** scientific rigor (35 %) — every claim in this report, with its registered prediction, its verdict and its entry. | claim | register id | verdict · confidence | entry | |---|---|---|---| | D1 yields no submittable drug and becomes the do-not table | H045 | supported · 0.80 | 113 | | D2 holds an approved compound with a molecule-level cell result | H046 | supported · 0.70 | 113 | | D3 has an approved route on the NAD⁺/SIRT2 axis with animal evidence, by proxy | H047 | supported · 0.60 | 113 | | D4 holds a non-chemotherapy approved drug at rung ≥ 2 with paediatric data | H048 | supported · 0.80 | 113 | | the automated stages are non-specific (D4 overlaps a decoy ≥ 0.10) | H049 | supported · 0.85 | 112 | | every argued drug has a paediatric pointer | H050 | supported · 0.70 | 113 | | the ladder is independent of the measured aneuploid fraction (card v4 moved no rung) | H061 | supported · 0.85 | 120 | | **the ladder is independent of the second instrument too** (card v5 moved no rung, no shortlist row, no do-not row — three unchanged digests) | **H065** | **supported · 0.90** | **133** | | no chromosome carries a mosaic aneuploidy above its own detection limit | H051 (step 8) | supported · 0.80 | 116 | | the detection limit is ≤ 10 % of cells for every autosome (measured 2–3 %) | H052 (step 8) | supported · 0.85 | 116 | | **the two aneuploidy instruments agree on every chromosome within their stated intervals** — the k-mer dosage route beside allele balance | **H054** (step 8) | **supported · 0.85** | **121, 123** | | the blind fused ranking put the confirmed pair first | H041/H043 (step 6) | see entries | 108–109 | | **the pipeline is portable to a different case *and* the spindle-poison caution fires there too** | **H066** | **refuted · 0.10** — written as a conjunction; 4 of 5 limbs held (including every portability limb), the caution limb failed because the pathway database returned nothing for the transfer gene. Recorded as refuted rather than reworded | **138** | | no approved drug acts directly on BubR1 | H011 (iteration 1) | supported · 0.80 | 078 | Confidence is a transparent triage heuristic printed with its arithmetic, never a probability. The register is append-only and shows every revision, including two committed too early and corrected in the open (entries 113 and 120) — and one claim, **H066**, that came back **refuted** and is reported as such rather than softened (§10).

register.statement: The disease mechanism in this proband is hypomorphic loss of BUB1B function: one null allele (stop_gained, exon 17 of 23) plus one partly functional allele (kinase-domain missense), leaving reduced BubR1 and a leaky spindle assembly checkpoint; there is no gain-of-function or dominant-negative component.

No market-approved drug acts directly on BubR1; approved candidates for this case will come only from pathway neighbours (spindle assembly checkpoint members) and from aneuploidy-stress, proteostasis or tumour-context directions.
The fused iteration-2 ranking places iteration 1's confirmed pair at rank 1, and no admitted ranking route places that pair below rank 3.
The fused leader is spoken for by at least two disjoint inputs once routes sharing an input are collapsed.

Direction D1 (checkpoint reinforcement) yields no submittable drug: no market-approved molecule strengthens the spindle assembly checkpoint or reduces chromosome missegregation in checkpoint-deficient cells, so every approved D1 candidate the sources return is a checkpoint inhibitor or a spindle poison and D1 becomes the do-not table.

Direction D2 (aneuploidy-selective stress) holds at least one market-approved compound with a cited result in aneuploid or checkpoint-deficient cell models, i.e. rung 2 or higher, and that evidence is for the approved molecule itself rather than only for an unapproved tool compound.

Direction D3 (BubR1 stabilisation for a hypomorph) has an approved-drug route: a market-approved agent acts on a BubR1-stabilising axis (SIRT2/NAD+ or acetylation) and the axis carries in-vivo evidence of raised BubR1 in a BubR1-insufficient model, i.e. rung 3, possibly through a same-axis proxy compound.

Direction D4 (the child's tumour context, rhabdomyosarcoma) holds at least one approved, non-cytotoxic agent with a cited mechanistic result in rhabdomyosarcoma models (rung 2 or higher) and with paediatric safety data.

The automated stages of the repurposing pipeline are not specific to the mechanism: with the clinical side held fixed and the gene swapped for a decoy (NTRK3, the seeded pick from the step-2 decoy set; XDH, an unrelated metabolic enzyme), at least one of the four directions' approved drug sets overlaps a decoy card's approved set at Jaccard 0.10 or more, so the curated rung, not the automated stage, is what separates candidates.

Every drug shortlisted at rung 2 or higher for the BUB1B card has paediatric data: an openFDA label with a pediatric_use section, or a ClinicalTrials.gov study that admits children, in any indication.
No chromosome in the sequenced sample -- autosome or X -- carries a mosaic aneuploidy at a cell fraction above its own measured detection limit.
The detection limit of the fold-over B-deviation test is at most 10 percent cell fraction for every autosome at this sample's heterozygous-site count and depth.
Fold-over B-deviation detects a mosaic gain at a materially lower cell fraction than the mean B-allele-fraction statistic entry 037 used, on identical simulated sites.
The k-mer dosage route and the VCF allele-balance route agree on every chromosome within their stated intervals.

The Track 2 drug-repurposing pipeline is portable to a different case, not only a different gene: a TRIP13 / mosaic variegated aneuploidy syndrome 3 transfer card - its own disease and identifiers, its own HPO terms read out of phenotype.hpoa, its own nephroblastoma tumour context and standard of care, no alleles and no curated evidence - runs through mva-drugs snapshot and the step-7 enrichment with no code change and no hand-written query; the checkpoint-reinforcement direction D1 again yields no submittable drug and every D1 row stays at rung 1, and the spindle-poison anti-direction A2 again populates the do-not table.

Iteration 4 goes from variant to mechanism to medicine using only its own evidence, in three stages, each a reusable tool with a provenance manifest. (1) Mechanism from five instruments that share no data: open variant-effect models run under one contract (AlphaMissense, ESM1b, REVEL place the missense allele in their top 0.47-2.59 %; GPN-MSA ranks the pair 508th of 54,865); a Boltz-2 fold of wild-type vs mutant BubR1 (inconclusive); a ThermoMPNN stability atlas of all 19,950 BubR1 substitutions, calibrated on published MVA allele classes before the child's allele was placed (the missense is at the 87th percentile, predicted destabilising); a phenotype twin that scores the child's 8 HPO terms against all 76,699 MGI mouse genotypes (a Bub1b hypomorph in the top 1.0-1.4 %, about 10x chance); and a gene ranking on the HPO terms (BUB1B 14th of 5,267). Reading: loss of function, too little stable BubR1. (2) Candidates from four generators whose rules were committed before any join: a PrimeKG walk from the MVA disease node (top 50 labelled drugs); the twin's published rescues (approved analogues: dasatinib, niacin); a screen-wide sweep of 613 approved drugs in PRISM for rhabdomyosarcoma- and aneuploidy-selective killing (top 0.5 % per contrast); and LINCS signature reversal of the BUB1B CRISPR-knockout signature in two engines (SigCom LINCS, iLINCS). Their agreement was tested against a 10,000-draw permutation null. (3) Three checks that can filter but never propose: direction (checkpoint-kinase inhibitors fail, measured in PRISM as less effective in aneuploid lines; spindle poisons a caution); the child's own safety from two sources side by side (PharmCAT/CPIC on the child's VCF, and OnSIDES/FAERS label effects matched to the child's HPO terms); and a contrary screen result. Result: 62 drugs; the generators agree on one, dasatinib, which is what chance gives (p 0.263); it passes every check. Every claim was registered before its test, and the refuted and uninterpretable ones are reported as such. The whole chain was re-run on a second disease (Bloom syndrome, BLM): it ran and proposed a different drug set (Jaccard 0.095), but needed a 378-line driver, so our claim that it moves by configuration alone is recorded as refuted.

Automated. Every candidate list comes from a generator rule written and committed before any join: a knowledge-graph walk (PrimeKG), a cross-species phenotype match over MGI with its published interventions, a screen-wide statistical sweep over PRISM, and connectivity queries to SigCom LINCS and iLINCS. The checks are automated too (PharmCAT, CPIC API, OnSIDES, openFDA FAERS). No LLM ranked or selected drugs.

Manual work is limited and recorded. (a) The phenotype twin's intervention table (12 rows) was read from paper abstracts, each with a verified PMID, and marks whether each rescue supports a direction. (b) The published MVA allele classes used to calibrate the stability atlas (8 alleles) were labelled from full texts with verbatim evidence (entry 149). (c) The mapping from the child's HPO terms to MedDRA adverse-effect terms is a hand-built, inspectable table (hpo_to_adverse_terms.tsv). (d) The report's wording and the direction table were written by hand from the entries. No candidate was added or removed by hand.
Publicly available sources only. No proprietary data source was used.

PrimeKG (Harvard Dataverse, CC0; DrugBank-derived drug nodes); openFDA drug labels and FAERS (public domain); MGI genotype-phenotype reports and the MP ontology, HPO and phenotype.hpoa, the Mouse-Human Mapping Initiative SSSOM (CC BY 4.0); PRISM Repurposing 24Q2 and 20Q2, DepMap 24Q4 model and omics signatures (CC BY 4.0, figshare mirrors, sha256 recorded); LINCS L1000 via SigCom LINCS and iLINCS; ChEMBL (max phase); the Drug Repurposing Hub mechanism labels shipped with PRISM; PharmCAT 3.4.0 with its bundled CPIC/DPWG/FDA annotations; the CPIC API; OnSIDES v3.1.1 (CC BY 4.0); AlphaFold DB (BubR1 model), UniProt, InterPro, CDD; ThermoMPNN (MIT); Boltz-2; AlphaMissense, ESM1b, REVEL, GPN-MSA, Evo 2, NT-v2, ESM-C score tables or models; PubMed (every cited PMID resolved via NCBI E-utilities).
None.

Loss of function, hypomorphic, of a compound heterozygote confirmed by the challenge's answer key: one stop_gained allele (no full-length protein) and one missense allele in BUB1B. The missense was read by five independent instruments: variant-effect models place it in their top 0.47-2.59 % and GPN-MSA ranks the pair at the 0.93rd percentile; a ThermoMPNN stability atlas puts it at the 87th percentile of all 19,950 possible substitutions, buried in the pseudokinase domain (predicted destabilising; the predictor could not separate published allele classes at n = 8, so the class is a prediction); a Boltz-2 fold is inconclusive; and the child's 8 clinical terms, independently of the genome, pick BubR1-deficient hypomorph mice from 76,699 genotypes. Pathway disrupted: the spindle assembly checkpoint (BubR1 is part of the mitotic checkpoint complex). Downstream consequence: chromosome mis-segregation and mosaic aneuploidy, with, in the twin mouse, early senescence, muscle wasting and growth failure, which match the child's terms. No evidence of gain of function or a dominant-negative protein.

Iteration 4's Track 2 steps (7, 9, 10, 11) ran from 2026-09-23 to 2026-09-25 on a laptop plus $14.59 of rented GPU (Modal) for the variant models, the Boltz-2 fold and the stability atlas. The drug stages cost $0 in compute: the phenotype twin runs in 53 s, the PRISM sweep in about 4 minutes, convergence and checks in 27 s, and the whole chain on the second disease in 53 minutes (most of it LINCS API queries).

Question. Given a confirmed compound-heterozygous loss of BUB1B (one stop_gained, one missense allele) in a child with mosaic variegated aneuploidy, rhabdomyosarcoma and growth failure, which approved drugs are plausible candidates, and which should be avoided? Approach. Iteration 4 rebuilt the answer from its own evidence only. The mechanism was read from five instruments that share no data: open variant-effect models, a structure predictor, a stability atlas of every possible BubR1 substitution calibrated on published allele classes, a phenotype twin matching the child's 8 HPO terms against all 76,699 MGI mouse genotypes, and a gene ranking on those terms. Candidates came from four generators whose rules were committed before any join: a PrimeKG walk, the twin's published rescues, a screen-wide PRISM sweep, and LINCS signature reversal. Their agreement was tested against a 10,000-draw permutation null. Three checks could only filter: mechanism direction, the child's own safety read from the genome (PharmCAT/CPIC) and the clinical terms (drug labels) side by side, and a contrary screen result. Every claim was registered with a prediction and a refutation condition before its run. Results. Mechanism: loss of function, too little stable BubR1; the missense is predicted destabilising (87th percentile ΔΔG) and the child's twin is a Bub1b hypomorph (top 1.0-1.4 %, about 10x chance). Drugs: 62 were named; the generators agree on one, dasatinib (a senolytic analogue of the rescue that delayed ageing in the twin, and 99.4th percentile for killing aneuploid lines), which is what chance gives (p 0.263, refuted as a convergence claim) but passes every check. Do not: checkpoint-kinase inhibitors, measured as less effective in 33 of 34 cases in aneuploid lines. For this child: the delivered callset answers 1.6 % of pharmacogene positions, so a targeted pharmacogenomic panel is the concrete request; vincristine is flagged by both safety sources; an incidental RYR1 call bears on anaesthesia. The chain ran on a second disease, Bloom syndrome, and proposed a different drug set, but only after a 378-line driver filled four case-specific gaps. Strengths. Independent instruments, pre-registration, a null for agreement, per-child safety from both data sources, full provenance, reusable tools, near-zero cost. Limitations. The drug list is thin and chance-level; two generators are weak (the screen finds nothing past correction; the expression generator failed its positive control); the mechanism class is predicted, not measured; the twin's rescues are genetic, not pharmacological; safety sources are often silent; nothing was tested in the child. These are hypotheses for follow-up, not treatment advice.
